In a small town nestled among the green hills of Ireland, a young man called Liam, struggling to find his place in the world, is stifled by the expectations of his family and community, who have it in their minds what he should be and do. But Liam has other ideas. One day, as he is walking along the banks of the river, he finds an old watch with a peculiar appearance. He opens it and finds it full of small stones of different shapes and sizes. The watch has a strange power, and Liam soon finds that it can transport him back in time to some significant moments in the lives of his ancestors. He is fascinated by the history of his family and tries to discover its secrets. He sees his great-grandfather, a stone-breaker, who toils and suffers in the quarries, and his grandmother, a young widow, raising her children after her husband’s death. And he sees his father trying to make a new life for himself and his family. Liam begins to understand the reasons why his family are the way they are, and it is their lives that help him to develop the empathy and compassion that will later enable him to face up to the problems he is facing himself. It is the wisdom he gains from this experience that will help him to take care of his loved ones without losing part of himself. And finally, he finds peace and a sense of belonging, and is at last connected to something that is bigger than himself: a family whose history is built on sacrifice, hope, love and endurance.

In the novel there is a boy named Dan Pussetto who attends a Catholic school in New York, which isn’t doing so well in sports or academics. His friend TJ Jones (also known as Tyler, the Trainer, or simply T) has the idea of starting a sport where everyone can participate, the Whalers Swim Club. You can see right away that the author is thinking of Moby Dick. Yet there are some who have read this book who still aren’t sure what it means. Everything depends on the context, doesn’t it? People take the text of the Gospel for granted, not noticing that we must place ourselves in the context of that text in order for it to have meaning.

This paper investigates how momentum contrast loss can help semi-supervised tasks for medical image segmentation. It has been shown that with two additional augmentations to an image (random rotation and Gaussian noise), deep learning can be learned without any supervision [7,8]. However, such methods depend on a specific noise level or augmentation, which might not be applicable to real world situations. To overcome this, we propose to use voxelwise prediction with a self-regularized loss. For example, given a noise level and rotation angle pair at time t, for each t, there are two samples, one reconstructed from the original noisy one with its ground truth, and another corrupted one with different noise scale or rotation angle, s_(t_1), with a predicted response, s_(t_1). As long as the semantic information is preserved after undergoing the above-mentioned transformation, it can serve as a suitable evaluation criterion. Each transformation is calculated by independent random parameters, uniformly distributed within the appropriate range. As a result, each transformation acts separately, and the network is less sensitive to external factors, so it is more robust to external factors. The MCL includes various regularizers, such as spatial consistency and spectral consistency. In each iteration, the MCL learns the best regularization terms according to the input characteristics of the image, so that the classification accuracy of the original input can be improved, and it is possible to compensate for the loss of the extraction of the feature extraction itself by sharing weights, before the convolution layer and so on. Figure 1: MCL with a self-regularized loss. The results in section 4 show that the proposed method achieves better results than the conventional method on a variety of settings, e.g., using only a small number of labeled data, and can achieve better results when more data is used to train the network.

The story of a mission to explore a newly discovered planet is full of suspense. The members of the crew, led by the invincible Captain Lei, have unique abilities and talents, and they are faced with many problems in space. Despite these obstacles, they are determined to complete the mission and discover the secrets of the planet. When they land on the planet, they are amazed by the discovery and find that they are not alone, and they have to struggle to protect their lives and mission against a hostile alien species. But with teamwork, courage, and wisdom, the crew is able to overcome all obstacles and successfully complete the mission, paving the way for future exploration and development.

In the little country town of Deogratias, a series of strange events has terrified the inhabitants. Unusual noises are heard at night and some animals have been found slaughtered in the fields. The villagers are convinced that a demon has taken possession of their town and turn to Father Ambrose for help and guidance. But Father Ambrose is battling his own demons and as the events escalate, he begins to doubt his faith and his ability to save his flock. In the meantime, the town’s mayor, Marcus, becomes obsessed with ridding Deogratias of its demonic blight. He leads a mob of townsfolk on a witch-hunt, suspecting everyone of being possessed. Accusations are made and false accusations fly. The town becomes divided, and Father Ambrose finds himself torn between his duty to protect his flock and his growing suspicion that the real evil is not something supernatural, but lies in the hearts of the villagers themselves. The climax of the story reaches a head, and Father Ambrose must choose between the forces of darkness and light. Will he be able to triumph over the darkness that is spreading through the town, or will he himself succumb to the darkness and become part of the evil? And in the meantime, the fate of Deogratias is hanging in the balance as the people await their salvation or their damnation.

The Charlier polynomials are a set of orthogonal polynomials arising in various mathematical and physical contexts, such as in quantum mechanics and statistical physics. In this paper we study the relations between the Charlier polynomials and the Hermite polynomials, which are another important family of orthogonal polynomials, with applications to many fields. We show that the transformation from the Charlier polynomials to the Hermite polynomials is a matter of a simple inverse multiplication; we find explicit formulas for the resulting polynomials. We also discuss some interesting properties of the transformed polynomials, such as their relationship with the Gaussian distribution and their use in digital signal processing. All in all, our results bring a new understanding of the structures and the behaviour of orthogonal polynomials, and may be useful in many scientific and technical applications.

This paper presents a new solution of the maximum flow problem, a fundamental problem of computer vision and image processing, in particular in the case of unsupervised image segmentation. This solution introduces a new type of estimation that improves the accuracy and speed of the maximum flow solution. This solution is based on a new mathematical model that takes into account the spatial and color information of the image, which increases the segmentation results. The efficiency of the proposed method has been tested in detail on different image sets, and its advantages are verified over existing methods in terms of accuracy and speed. This study opens up new possibilities for developing more advanced unsupervised image segmentation methods.

In this paper we explore the use of information-theoretical bounds as a means of analyzing superconformal field theory. In particular, we investigate the concept of mutual information, which quantifies the amount of information that can be extracted from one system about another, and we show that mutual information can be used to bound the entropy of a superconformal system. We discuss the implications of this bound for the study of black holes and other extreme objects in superconformal field theory. Generally, our results give a new perspective on the relationship between information theory and superconformal field theory and open up further avenues of research.

The study of the behaviour of the valence and conduction bands in crystalline semiconductors is one of the great problems of condensed matter physics. This paper provides a review of the present knowledge of the interactions between the valence and conduction bands, with particular emphasis on the role played by the crystalline lattice, and of the different theoretical models used to explain their properties. They also discuss the different experimental methods employed to study them, such as photoemission, scanning tunnelling microscopy and angle-resolved photoemission. Finally they examine recent progress in the field, such as the discovery of new materials, the study of topological insulators and the exploitation of new devices based on heterostructures of crystalline semiconductors.

Amidst the picturesque surroundings of a little town in the countryside, a heavy atmosphere reigns among the inhabitants. The local factory, the town's main source of employment, has been closed for several months now because of a mysterious accident. The inhabitants struggle to make ends meet, and their nerves are becoming taut. Amidst this social unrest, a group of strangers arrives in town. Each has his own secrets and his own motives, but they all want to find out the truth behind the factory's closure. There is a young journalist, Alice, who has been sent from the city to cover the story but who soon finds herself entangled in it. There is a former worker at the factory, a former local boy, who has returned to his hometown, is haunted by a tragedy that happened there, and is determined to discover the reason for the factory's closure. Then there is Maria, a shy scientist who has been studying the local fauna and has made some startling discoveries. It is she who links the factory's mysterious closure with a series of bizarre occurrences in the woods surrounding the town. As the outsiders delve deeper into the mystery, the resulting tension rises and the group discovers the secret to the town's isolation. It becomes clear that the factory's closure is only the tip of the iceberg and that the town is harbouring a dark and dangerous secret. As the stakes become higher, the group has to come together, facing their own demons and the increasing danger, to confront the truth before it is too late. The truth, which they uncover, will change the town forever. Will they be able to reveal the conspiracy before it is too late, or will they be made the next victims of it?

At the time when human beings have expanded to fill the entire universe, an event known only as “The End” has brought the total disappearance of all life. Planets, stars, and even space have been destroyed, and what remains is a vast void. This is the story of a small group of survivors who find themselves stranded on a small isolated planet which somehow managed to avoid destruction. Under the leadership of a young woman named Ava, they are tasked with the task of surviving in a world where resources have run out, the laws of physics no longer apply, and the very nature of reality has been distorted. They come across strange objects and clues which make them realize that the true cause of the disaster was not what they thought, but that they are not alone in their search for the truth, and that others have a wealth of knowledge and power beyond their imagination. During their travels through the void, they encounter terrifying new beings, ancient civilizations, and advanced technology which force them to question their understanding of the universe. Then, as they delve deeper into the mysteries of The End, they come to realize that their true enemy is not the void, but the darkness that lies within the human heart. The catastrophe has brought human beings to the brink of self-destruction, and in the darkness they must face the horrors that they have unleashed. The group must choose, and Ava and her companions must decide whether they will allow themselves to be destroyed by the darkness, or they will find a way to conquer it and restore light to the universe. In the balance hangs the fate of humankind. The future is uncertain.

This paper presents a hierarchical move-making method for optimizing general pairwise non-submodular energies. The approach consists of dividing the problem into different layers to enable efficient exploration and exploitation of potential moves at different granularities. Then we analyze its performance on various benchmark data. This paper contributes to the development of an effective way of optimizing complex energy functions in machine learning and artificial intelligence.

We have shown that liquid water is able to exist at a surface because of its conductive nature (the heat of vaporization), which means that the single molecules of the fluid detach from the surface by convection. This, in turn, produces convection and convection at the surface, and even convection of the water at a surface. The same effect occurs behind a glass. On both sides of a glass there are many, many air bubbles. Depending on their size, they are spaced more closely, because they are melting into each other, until one or two bubbles grow so big that they erupt through the glass and become rain. The physics is from our model: A large surface can form a large liquid if you can produce convection of the small molecules on the micro-scale inside the glass of a refrigerator or a frost hole in the icebox, where the small volume difference produces a lot of convection, like we see when an air bubble hits a water surface. Our model corresponds to this idea very well, though there is nothing to stop water rising to meet water or vice versa! But there must be something else going on too, and it would be nice if we had found that instead!

This article is about the Lie algebras of differential operators and their extensions, the properties of which are treated, as well as their applications in mathematics, physics, and engineering. It presents a complete and methodical view of the theory and application of extensions of differential operators.

Here is the abstract for the abstract for "Automatic Measurement of Head Coating Thickness with the Large-Device Neural Net": Head-covering thickness is an important parameter in the characterization of magnetic tapes. The HOC thickness is usually measured manually, which is time-consuming and prone to errors. In this paper, a method of automatic HOC thickness measurement using the large-device neural net is presented. The method uses a trained convolutional neural network to extract the HOC thickness from a tape image. The network is trained using a large set of images and HOC thickness values, and then used to predict the HOC thickness from an image. Our method is accurate, automatic, and efficient and can be used to replace the current manual method.

In this book we learn the truth behind 'Wicked' and the mechanism of its activities. We also see what lies beyond the electric barrier of the camp's terminal 631. Crank/Minho, having escaped from the camp, rescued Thomas, Jorge, Chuck, Aris, and Newt, but lost the others. After having gone through a hostile desert, a place where they were being pursued by the dreaded “cranks,” people whose bodies had been mutated by the lethal “cranks” — a deadly, mutated, insect-like swarm — Thomas felt a strange attraction to Chuck, who was also a human being, though his body had been partially mutated by cockroach-like arms and other limbs. He grew to like Chuck, despite his distrust of him as a traitor. But when she was caught trying to save his life, he started searching for her in the desert. They were caught and locked up in some place by the organization called “Wicked.” Among those locked up was a woman who resembled Teresa, a girl he had met at the camp. Now he believed that she was the chief of a secret, evil organization called “Wicked.” It turns out that these places were death traps. But some of them escaped, gathered together, and tried to salvage their lives by a guide, only to encounter yet another trial gone wrong. But this time, they gathered all their courage to face the trial and also found some clues to the mystery. Suddenly, two figures approached among the ruins, one of whom had a similar scar to the one on Teresa at terminal 3073. She was careful not to move and, as she approached, the two talked with each other. But what was her true purpose? Or does she still have something that is far more terrible than anything she has ever been frightened of? What fate awaits them this time? I can't answer these questions, but you can read it and find out. Today is the day to find out.

Post-mortem iris recognition is a challenging task in biometrics due to the degradation and variability in the images. Deep learning has recently been found to be successful in addressing the challenges of iris recognition. In this paper, we propose a new method for post-mortem iris recognition that combines the advantages of deep learning and the performance of classical machine learning. Our method first uses a deep learning model to segment the iris region from images, and then it uses several classical machine learning methods to recognize the iris patterns. We show that our method can achieve higher accuracy than other methods on high-quality iris images and that it is able to generalize well to low-quality images that are often encountered in post-mortem iris recognition.

This paper presents a novel approach to brain tumor detection based on symmetry information. Taking advantage of the symmetrical nature of the human brain, our method employs image processing methods to analyze the symmetry information extracted from a magnetic resonance image (MRI). As compared to other methods, this approach can potentially enhance the sensitivity and reduce the number of false positives. This method has been tested on several sets of data and shows a high degree of sensitivity in detecting brain tumors.

This article presents a study of the methods of solving multiple binomials, which are expressions which include the sum of the products of binomials, with the purpose of illustrating the historical development of these methods, as well as presenting the most recent applications to various mathematical fields such as probability theory, combinatorics, and cryptography. We discuss a number of methods based on the use of combinations, generating functions, and algebraic manipulation, and we illustrate these methods with examples. We also indicate some possible directions for further research. In a general way, this work provides a valuable insight into methods of efficiently solving complex polynomials, which arise often in the study of mathematical modeling.

The article explores the Snow Leopard Permutations and their strange properties, especially with their even and odd threads. Snow Leopard Permutations are a new concept in permutations and have been shown to have many applications in mathematics and computer science. In this article, we examine the properties of Snow Leopard Permutations and their relationship to their even and odd threads. We find that Snow Leopard Permutations can be divided into even and odd Snow Leopard Permutations. Even Snow Leopard Permutations have the property that the number of inversions in the permutation is even, and odd Snow Leopard Permutations have the property that the number of inversions is odd. We also show that the number of even Snow Leopard Permutations and odd Snow Leopard Permutations with the same length are always equal, and the generation of even Snow Leopard Permutations and odd Snow Leopard Permutations with the same length can be achieved with a novel efficient method. Furthermore, we study the relationship between Snow Leopard Permutations and other well-known concepts in combinatorics, such as Catalan numbers and Fibonacci numbers. The results show that Snow Leopard Permutations have a close relationship with them and can provide new insights into their properties. This has important implications for the development of combinatorics and the theory of computation. In particular, the Snow Leopard Permutation can be used to explain a wide range of problems in coding theory and cryptography. In summary, the Snow Leopard Permutation and its even and odd threads have been further explored, and the properties of Snow Leopard Permutations have been extended to more general numbers. The results shed new light on combinatorics and can provide a useful tool for the study of many problems.

Our paper presents a self-supervised deep learning algorithm for the automatic construction of images from a robot camera. In contrast to other methods, which require the manual construction of images of surgical instruments for visualization, our method generates annotations by itself. In particular, we present a method of composing and registering images of a robot surgical arm automatically, thus enabling the vision-based autonomy of robot surgery. Because manual annotations are difficult and time-consuming and because surgical instruments move, we developed a self-supervised method. We present a deep learning-based image composition method and we use camera poses for registration. Our method outperforms the visual tracking methods, which are designed for the visual tracking of surgical instruments, in terms of speed and simplicity. We compare our method with the state-of-the-art method for estimating the pose of a camera and show the application examples. In addition, as an important step towards future research, we present an automatic method for recognizing surgical instruments on images taken by a robot camera.

CRFs are usually implemented using carefully designed hand-crafted features, resulting from unstructured learning. Recently, neural networks have been used to model the learning of potentials. This is based on the observation that instead of handcrafting features and learning them separately, it is more efficient to use a neural network that can learn features together, both unary and pairs. This paper proposes to develop a method for learning a potential by unsupervised learning (with the help of a convolutional network). Conditional random fields (CRFs) have been a common choice for the task of predicting objects in structured settings, like object detection and segmentation. There are different types of potentials in CRFs, e.g., first order, second order, linear, nonlinear. The potentials provide local structure to the prediction task, but they are usually limited by prior knowledge and domain design. Recently, the trend has been to use the features obtained from the neural network to construct the potential. The typical method is to train a deep network like a convolutional network by a supervised classification task, and then use the features obtained from the supervised training to construct the potential. Deep CRFs [8–10] are capable of learning unary and pairwise potentials together. The success of such an approach is limited by the choice of features that are required for a large amount of labeled data. Recent studies in unsupervised learning have shown great success in learning structured pairwise features, such as for multi-instance learning [11,12] and other tasks. The use of unlabeled data greatly reduces the amount of labeled data. The graphical models in the CRF models described above are limited to learning first and second order graphical models, where the pairwise features are first order Gaussian mixtures of single features. Unlabeled learning is more ideally used to learn the pairwise features and the unary features. But learning the higher order potentials with unsupervised learning is not straightforward because the potentials are not easily obtained.

Jonathan is not just an ordinary gull. He has a philosophical outlook that is quite different from the other seagulls. He doesn’t simply eat up all the food his mother, Giselle, throws to him and try to survive as the other gulls do, but he aspires to perfect his flight, an ambition that is usually found only in human beings or Greek gods. He tries various tricks, such as catching insects in mid-air before they can land, which is both hard on the insects and sad on his part. If all seagulls did this, there would soon be no more birds. “You should not think so highly of people,” says his mother, who feels sorry for him, but there are always some who try to help him, so he decides to get some training and tries to make it a bit better by catching other seagulls, and so on. This is a more difficult trick than catching other seagulls, but he learns to do it by feeling sorry for them, which is an excellent accomplishment. However, this is not good enough for Otsune. He tries to catch some other seagulls with his beak, tries to copy the flight of a bird with wings like an eagle, attacks other seagulls with his beak, makes a leaping upwards like an eagle, and develops new skills.

The paper is entitled "RatLesNetv2: Fully Convolutional Network for Brain Lesions Segmentation in Mouse Images", by Y. Chen et al., published in the Bioinformatics Journal, Volume 15, Issue 14, pages 2289–2295, October, 2018. The paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of the network's performance and demonstrates its capability for the automatic analysis of brain lesions in mouse images.

This story is based in the town of Millerville, a little town, almost a village, in the heart of the countryside. It seems a peaceful little place where everyone knows each other and where there is almost no crime. But behind this apparent simplicity is a tangled web of lies and secrets that threatens to undermine the whole structure of the society. The main character of the story is Sarah, a young woman who has just inherited the farm from her parents, following their tragic death. She struggles to deal with the death of her parents and tries to keep herself together, but then she finds out that her mother’s death was no accident. She sets out on a dangerous quest for the truth and for justice for her father. But when she starts digging into the past of Millerville, she discovers a history of betrayal and deceit that goes beyond her own family. She uncovers the carefully concealed secrets of some of the most powerful people in the town and pushes them to the brink of ruin, while making allies and enemies at the same time. When everything starts to go terribly wrong, she must decide whether to continue her quest for the truth or to protect the ones she loves from the disastrous consequences, while everything around her is crumbling to pieces.

In the co-segmentation of images, the divisions of two or more images are made simultaneously; and this is useful in recognizing objects in different pictures. As the knowledge of the phenomenon of vision is becoming more and more complete, there is a greater desire to find methods of treating it mechanically, without manual intervention. This survey presents an overview of the current state of the art of automatic image co-segmentation, both in terms of traditional methods and deep learning. First of all, we discuss the basic concepts of image co-segmentation, namely the different types of co-segmentation and the difficulties of this task. Secondly, we review the old methods of image co-segmentation, such as feature, skeleton and graph. Thirdly, we study in detail the deep learning methods, such as convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, and generative adversarial networks. These methods are able to extract complex features and patterns from a large number of images, and have achieved excellent results in image co-segmentation. Finally, we also discuss the evaluation metrics for image co-segmentation, and the publicly available data and benchmarks that can be used to test these methods. This survey concludes with an overview of the current limitations and difficulties in co-segmentation, and with the future directions of research. This survey gives a clear overview of the state-of-the-art methods for automatic image co-segmentation, and is useful for both theoreticians and practitioners in this field.

This paper presents a gradient vector flow based shape prior for the best segmentation of multiple objects. The proposed gradient vector flow shape prior overcomes the limitations of the traditional shape priors by providing a more flexible and effective shape representation. The proposed gradient vector flow shape prior is used in combination with a new energy function to obtain the best segmentation of multiple objects. The new energy function minimizes a combination of region competition, color likelihood, and the proposed gradient vector flow based shape prior. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods for multiple object segmentation.

This paper describes a novel method of dividing images into their constituent parts, based on the combined sparse-to-variation and tv-minimax tv-minimax methods. Using sparse constraints on the coefficients of each pixel, the resulting model can effectively separate complex backgrounds from foreground objects or text. Total variation regularization in the objective function ensures smooth transitions between regions and preserves important details and edges. Our experiments show that our method outperforms existing methods, and makes it a suitable tool for various applications, such as the analysis of surveillance images, special effects in film and television and digital signwriting. In general, our method is an efficient and reliable way of partitioning screen images, with minimal human intervention.

This article discusses witness structures, which are topological spaces which help to understand the algebraic properties of a space. Then it deals with snapshot complexes, which are a method of further investigation of the witness structures, by providing information about their geometric structure at certain instants of time. Both concepts are discussed with mathematical accuracy, and various applications of them are mentioned.

Orthopedic surgery and radiology are very much dependent on the use of computer-aided knee-joint MR segmentation. The present paper is an overview of MR knee joint segmentation methods and focuses on the knee joint. It discusses various approaches to knee joint segmentation, such as manual, semi-automatic and automatic methods. It also includes the recent advances in deep learning and convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which have shown great promise for improving the accuracy and efficiency of knee joint MR segmentation. It also points out the challenges and future prospects for knee joint MR segmentation, such as variability in anatomy and artifacts. This overview serves as a guide for both practitioners and researches interested in knee joint MR segmentation.

In this paper we construct an infinite number of zeros of high derivatives of the Riemann zeta-function by means of a certain number-theoretic conjecture. We also conjecture the existence of an explicit sequence of such zeros, and prove this conjecture in certain aspects. In semi-supervised learning, the supervised model (SVM) has been used to classify the entire training image in the same space, which is not a very interesting case. In this paper, we propose a novel method to automatically learn a contrastive gradient-guided feature representation (CGPR), which can facilitate the learning of a wide range of models, including a variety of multiclass SVMs that require the same input space to be learned over several epochs. Compared with the conventional SVM method (Cf. ), the CGPR method has the following advantages: it is low-dimensional (which is conducive to low-cost training), does not introduce over-fitting, and can be used for gradient-guided learning. It is a self-supervised learning method, and the SVM method has been used to do this, but it has not been used in a deep learning model until recently (Cf. )., [16]),[17],[18]] and the residual method of the CGPR is introduced. We also show that a new class of SVMs can be learned with a CGPR method. Then we show a variety of applications, such as medical image segmentation, which can only be learned by fully labeled images.

This paper introduces a new class of Nikishin systems, with periodic recurrence coefficients, which generalize the classical periodic Nikishin system. We investigate the asymptotic behaviour of these systems with respect to large values of N. We show that the number of states of the Markov partition of the system, divided by N, converges to a well-defined limit as N tends to infinity. The limits we obtain satisfy the so-called Weiss conjecture, which ensures the convergence of the corresponding entropy function. Our results demonstrate that, for the periodic case, the recurrence coefficients of the system impose an ergodic structure on the state space, which can be described in terms of the Weiss conjecture. We prove our results by combining the classical Nikishin method with Markov-partition techniques.

This paper describes an active set algorithm for the estimation of the order-dependent parameters in a generalized linear model. The algorithm is designed to deal with situations where the number of predictors is large and the predictors are ordered. The active set is iteratively refined and the parameters are estimated by a modified Newton-Raphson method. The performance of the method is evaluated by simulation and compared with existing methods. The simulations indicate that the proposed method is accurate and efficient. In general, the active set method is useful for estimating order-dependent parameters in a generalized linear model.

First published by Ace Books in 1978, it is set in the same world as his previous book, Titan, and is also the story of a character called Joe Santa Maria. They are trying to create a human who is smarter and more physically capable than the four previous human species. The book explores themes of identity, evolution and the nature of humanity. It is an enjoyable and thought-provoking novel, and is considered one of Varley’s best works. Random forest is widely used in many pattern recognition applications, but the method has some disadvantages. First, it is very difficult to calculate the split points from the entire training set. Second, the initial random subset is a problem that makes the random tree slow, and may cause overfitting when the data set is large. The FRF classifier is proposed in this paper to solve these problems, and the split points of each tree are calculated according to the random subset of the data. Moreover, the random forest method is combined with the deep convolutional neural network (CNN) to map the original feature to the higher feature, and then calculate the split points. The simulation results show that the FRF method can improve the classification accuracy.

IGRAINNE THE BRAVE is the story of a young woman named IGRAINNE, who lives in a country where reigns a tyrant. IGRAINNE’S FATHER, A knight and nobleman, and the father of IGRAINNE, is a dissenter to the tyrant and is seized by him and imprisoned. IGRAINNE’S PUNY LUST is to save her father and put down the king. She gathers together a company of rebels, and thence they go on a perilous voyage, with battles, perils, and unexpected allies. IGRAINNE finds her own strength and courage, and is a new hope to the people of the land. At last she conquers the king, and her father, and restores peace and right to the kingdom.

This paper is concerned with developing and applying a calibrated surrogate maximization method based on linear fractional utility functions to classification problems. The goal of the method is to optimize for accuracy and efficiency simultaneously by using an adaptive calibration technique that limits overfitting and improves decision-making performance. Extensive experiments have shown that this method has better performance than the methods currently used and that it can be implemented at a reasonable cost. It can be seen, therefore, that this method offers the possibility of solving a wide variety of multiclass classification problems that involve conflicting objectives.

— With this paper, we address the problem of image segmentation with noisy annotations, which occurs in real applications due to the expensive and laborious labeling procedure. We propose a novel method for distilling effective supervision from a small number of annotated images by a technique called noisy label refinement. Our method is based on the insight that despite the noise, the labels of a small number of carefully chosen images can be used to train a robust model for segmentation. We show the effectiveness of our method on three public medical image segmentation tasks, where we achieve state-of-the-art results, while using only a small portion of the available annotated images. Our results demonstrate that our method reduces the influence of noise and improves the accuracy of segmentation.

In this paper, we introduce MultiResUNet, a multi-modal, biomedical image-segmentation framework. It was designed to address the limitations of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures, which struggle with multi-modal images, large datasets, and transfer learning. MultiResUNet takes components of the popular U-net network and modifies them so that it can efficiently encode multi-modality while remaining compact. We show that our approach is effective on three publicly available breast-cancer datasets. Our model is able to achieve the same level of performance as U-net but takes up to four times less memory. We then conduct a thorough analysis of the advantages of our model over other architectures in terms of generalization, sensitivity to multi-modality, and the ability to benefit from transfer learning. To the best of our knowledge, ours is the first paper to explicitly investigate and measure the impact of architecture design on multi-modal performance and transfer learning. The code is available at https://github.com/newvalue/MultiResUNet.

This paper is a comprehensive review of recent progress in knee joint magnetic resonance image segmentation, addressing the major challenges faced and the most recent advances in this area. The methods covered include thresholding, region growing, clustering, active contours, deep learning methods, and hybrid methods. Each approach is analyzed with respect to its accuracy, efficiency, robustness, and automation level. We discuss the current limitations of the methods, and future directions for research in this area. The goal is to provide the reader with a broad perspective on the current trends in knee joint MRI segmentation, in order to provide the necessary foundation for the development of advanced tools for orthopedic and diagnostic imaging.

The life of a young woman named Isabel, who has the power of destroying her own memories and thus her identity. She has no memory of her past, and the present is filled with disconnected images and memories that she cannot unite. In spite of this, she has an incredible gift for painting, which makes her a star in the world of painting. The further the film goes, the more obsessed with discovering her identity and past, the more she starts to doubt everything about it. This leads her into dangerous paths, to mysterious people, to concealed documents and riddles. With each new discovery, the doubts grow, until she becomes confused between two different versions of reality. However, a powerful group, called the patrons, also notices Isabel's extraordinary gift and wants to use her for their own purposes, whatever they are. They don't spare themselves, resorting to violence and murder to keep her. So Isabel must make the most difficult decisions, with dangerous allies and thorny contradictions, in order to preserve her identity. The only way to escape the clutches of the patrons lies in the recollected images and the shadows of the past. But the price is higher than she can pay. Will she be able to solve the mystery of her past before she becomes a victim, or will she fall prey to the threatening powers?

This paper will provide an overview of the dielectric properties of a variety of materials, including the band gap, dielectric constant and thermal stability, and will show how these properties affect the properties of van der Waals heterostructures, such as optical and electrical properties. Furthermore, we will emphasize the difficulties and advantages of using different dielectric materials in these structures, and give guidance on the choice of dielectric materials for a particular application. In summary, this paper provides a comprehensive overview of the dielectric foundations of van der Waals heterostructures, and serves as a useful guide for research in this field.

The parasite is an intelligent being that feeds on a parasitic species that has consumed 90 per cent of its food-source to obtain sustenance and reproduction, without finding any other living organism in its local environment capable of supplying it with the nourishment necessary for such a parasitic relationship.

Search and rescue is the task of rescuing persons in danger, often in a complicated and often large amount of data. Small target detection is a key step in search and rescue to find and identify a person in a complex and cluttered environment. This paper presents a deep learning-based approach for small target detection by means of artificially generated data and distributed computation. We first generate synthetic images of people in various environments with a ray tracing tool, and then use convolutional neural networks to train small target detection models on the synthetic images, and then deploy the convolutional neural networks on a cluster for increased speed and accuracy. We evaluate our method on real-world data and show that it achieves a better performance than previous approaches. The results of the experiments show that our method can improve search and rescue, save time and save lives in critical situations.

Having omitted to mention that the purpose of this chapter is to develop a new method of classification and delineation of the various tumours and diseases. It is based on a combination of unsupervised and supervised learning, and is designed to improve the accuracy and interpretability of the model. The unsupervised learning is based on the idea that the unlabelled data set can be used to generate useful representations, which can then be used to improve the performance of a supervised learning model. The sample selection is based on the idea that it is possible to select the best subset of the training set for improving the interpretability of the model. The proposed method is applied to the task of classifying and delineating the skin lesions. The results show significant improvements in accuracy and interpretability compared to previous methods.

The abstract of the article titled “One system to sever the matter all” is as follows: this paper presents a new system based on deep learning for a general 3D medical image segmentation, the proposed system uses a single convolutional neural network to segment many organs and tissues, without the need to create a separate network for each organ, and the proposed network is light and efficient, a small number of parameters, a short training time. The system is trained with a large number of 3D medical images, and it achieves state-of-the-art performance on several typical benchmarks.

This paper continues our study on the occurrence of 'drop-outs' in multicell coordinated beamforming. It is shown that by using certain outage probability, the transmitted power of a multicell system can be minimized. In this paper, a two-step approach is presented which first solves a relaxed problem and then refines the solution to ensure the outage probability constraints. The proposed method provides near-optimal solutions with much reduced complexity. Extensive simulations confirm the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed methods.

UNET++ is a novel deep-learning network architecture designed for the purpose of segmenting medical images, extending the original U-Net network by nesting. This neural network model consists of multiple encoder-decoder blocks, each of which contains a series of convolutional layers, followed by batch normalization and rectified linear unit (ReLU) functions. Each of these blocks is connected in a hierarchical manner, the output of the previous one being incorporated into the next one, and so on. The main innovation of UNET++ is its ability to process large and complex medical images, which are usually characterized by rich details and complex structures, and can be difficult to capture by using conventional neural networks. However, using the power of convolutional neural networks, UNET++ can automatically learn and extract these features from the input image, enabling it to achieve excellent performance in a variety of medical-imaging tasks. UNET++ is an important achievement in the field of medical image segmentation, and will give clinicians and medical scientists a powerful tool for accurately identifying and isolating features in complex images.

This dissertation is a study of the influence of small random perturbations on dynamic systems. We study the long-term effects of these perturbations and whether they lead to a stationary state. Through a series of mathematical studies and numerical experiments, we attempt to clarify the mechanism of thermalization and the conditions under which it can occur. The results of this work are applicable to many different fields including physics, engineering, and computer science, and contribute to our overall understanding of complex systems and their behavior.

This paper proposes a novel self-learning artificial intelligence (AI) for advanced segmentation and classification of skin lesions in dermoscopy images. Our unique approach enhances the ability of convolutional neural networks to recognize skin lesions, resulting in increased diagnostic accuracy. An important feature of our method is its self-learning capability whereby the AI system can continually learn and improve its diagnostic accuracy by importing new images and patient data. In addition, we evaluated our framework using a standard image dataset and it showed superior performance compared to existing methods. Therefore, our AI system is of significant value in early and accurate detection of skin cancers, thereby increasing the survival rates of patients.

This paper discusses the uncertainties associated with the Sunspot Number, the estimates of its variability and their implications for our understanding of the Sun's activity and its effects on climate. The Sunspot Number is the most frequently used index of solar activity, but it has been affected by different sources of uncertainty over its history, such as variations in observational technique, instrumentation and in the interpretation of data. By combining historical records with modern data analysis methods, we estimate the variability of Sunspot Number and its variation over time and space. Our results indicate that the Sunspot Number is not without uncertainty, varying between 10 and 30 per cent, depending on the period and observatory. We also find that these uncertainties change over time, with higher values of uncertainty in times of low activity. The implications of these uncertainties are profound, as they not only affect our understanding of the Sun's past activity, but also our ability to predict its future activity and its possible effects on climate. Moreover, the Sunspot Number is used in forecasting space weather, such as coronal mass ejections and geomagnetic storms, which affect the operation of satellites, communication systems and power grids. This paper therefore highlights the need to continue to improve the accuracy and consistency of sunspot observations and to better understand the causes of the uncertainty. By doing so, we can enhance our knowledge of the Sun's activity and its effects on climate, and hence our ability to predict and prepare for potentially harmful space weather events.

The presence of an inconsistent number of annotated anatomical landmarks in an annotated cardiac MR image can result in a deficiency of the automatic results of the NST. The following paper reports a study on the effect of an inconsistent annotated image on NST. We find that an inconsistent annotated image leads to a deficiency of the NST and we analyze the reasons for this phenomenon. We propose a simple but effective solution to correct the NST by identifying and removing inconsistent regions of the manual annotated style. We show the improved performance of the proposed method compared to the state-of-the-art in two public MR image datasets. Our code is available at https://github.com/CristianRC/NST-Segmentation.

LooseCut is a new method for creating a coarse model of an object. Existing methods often rely on small boxes, which lead to great frustration in fine-tuning them. LooseCut, on the other hand, is based on a new strategy of loosely bounding boxes, which make the object easier to find. Our method takes advantage of the recent advances in deep learning based segmentation and integrates a novel optimization mechanism that improves the initial box by iteratively refining it with the help of the user. We compare LooseCut to several challenging datasets and demonstrate that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both efficiency and accuracy. We also performed a small user study to test the effectiveness and usability of our approach in real-world cases. Our main contributions can be summarized as follows: 1. Introduce LooseCut, an interactive method for image segmentation based on loose bounding boxes. 2. Development of a novel mechanism for iteratively refining initial boxes with the help of the user. 3. Comparison of LooseCut with existing methods on various image datasets. 4. A comprehensive user study to verify the usability and effectiveness of LooseCut. Our method has a strong potential to improve the interactive segmentation of images in various applications, such as object recognition, object tracking and medical image analysis.

A layered neural network has been used to determine the best matching of the image with the search words in semantic image segmentation. An unsupervised approach with no experimental verification, revealed the highest success rate for a layered neural network with two hidden layers. The two-layer architecture has shown good performance in the case where the matching of high-level features is performed with a high degree of confidence, and where the matching of features is rather coarse, because of the poor resolution of the image. However, the architecture is highly scalable, because of its high accuracy in the classification of images from a wide range of real-world content, but also due to its low memory requirements, compared to a fully convolutional architecture. Moreover, whereas only one layer of the neural network was successful in the learning of a general classifier, all of the layers of the deep net independently acquired new features. Therefore, it is concluded that each layer has a distinct task, which can be accomplished by a different recurrent network architecture. Thus, a great many types of learning algorithms may be combined in future.

– Abstract: We present a fully automatic proofreader that corrects common errors made in the neural data segmentations produced by state-of-the-art brain image analysis pipelines. Our method uses reinforcement learning to learn how to correct the most frequent mistakes made by manual proofreaders, and then applies these corrections automatically. In experiments with one thousand neuronal samples labelled by a human expert as part of the Allen-Mouse-CCF project, we show that our method outperforms human performance with respect to both accuracy and speed.

Self-Ensembling Contrastive Learning is a new method of semi-supervised learning for medical image segmentation that exploits the combination of several different learning models, each of which has learned from a different subset of the data. Training several models simultaneously with different parameters and input features provides a self-ensembling mechanism that allows the model to learn from both supervised and unsupervised examples, thus improving the accuracy and robustness of the model. It was tested on two publicly available datasets: MIMIC-III and Chest-X-Ray,14 and it was compared with other methods in the state of the art. Its results were superior to those of the other methods and the model showed a strong generalization ability. In general, this paper provides a method of self-ensembling contrastive learning as a powerful tool for improving the accuracy and robustness of medical image segmentation.

We consider the interference of a single and two photons in a polariton-coupled interferometer, in which one of the arms contains a nonlinear Kerr medium. It is found that the visibility of the two-photon interference is decreased by the presence of the nonlinearity, whereas the visibility of the single-photon interference is not affected by the presence of the nonlinearity. This result is explained by the fact that the nonlinearity breaks the symmetry between the two arms of the interferometer, causing the two-photon interference to have a different phase shift. In particular, we also find that the visibility of the two-photon interference is smaller when the nonlinearity is increased, while the visibility of the single-photon interference is not changed.

In the age of the digital, the concept of collective memory has changed in a way that includes new forms of media and new ways of remembering. This article examines the nature of collective memory in the digital age, and the relationship between digital memory and collective memory. Through a critical analysis of various platforms such as social media, digital archives and digital museums, it examines how digital memory and its relationships with digital memory and how it may affect our society. In the era of the digital, digital memory offers unprecedented opportunities to preserve and share cultural heritage, but at the same time, it brings about a new dilemma for collective memory. Taking into account the issues of data privacy, the prejudices of search engines, and the temporality of digital memories, this article outlines a framework for a new way of understanding collective memory in the era of the digital. This article contributes to the existing body of knowledge by offering a new understanding of the role of technology in the construction of collective memory and collective identity, and offers a few strategies for promoting diverse, pluralistic digital collective memories that reflect the complexities of human experience.

This paper proposes a new method for automatically determining the thickness of a cape. The technique overcomes the shortcomings of the old method, which was usually manual and time-consuming. The NASNet-large-decoder network, using a convolutional neural network, can process the input image and accurately determine the thickness of the cape. It is based on a large number of images taken by an atomic force microscope, and the corresponding model has been trained, and the decoding accuracy is very high. The application value of this method is mainly in the hard disk industry and other fields where accurate thickness measurement is required.

"In this paper we propose a new method of belief propagation, called sigma-point belief propagation. Belief propagation is an important method in machine learning and artificial intelligence which enables the derivation of marginal probability in a complex graphical model., but traditional belief propagation has two main drawbacks: it becomes too cumbersome when dealing with large graphs, and it cannot represent complex interdependencies between the elements. SBA fixes these two problems by using a novel probabilistic representation based on sigma-points, a generalization of Gaussian distributions, which allows efficient and accurate representation of complex distributions and inference on large graphs. We present an experimental evaluation of the method on a set of well-known data sets and compare its performance with other well-known belief propagation methods." In addition, the theoretical properties of the method are analyzed and the complexity is estimated. The paper also presents some interesting applications in the field of computer vision, natural language processing and decision analysis. In general, our paper is a major development in the field of belief propagation and opens up new possibilities for solving difficult problems in machine learning and artificial intelligence.

The correct positioning of the dental root is essential to the success of root canal treatment. But due to the small size and low contrast of the dental root, it is difficult to be separated from the visual image by simple division, especially the fuzzy boundary of the dental root, which is difficult to be obtained by a single-linear method. There have been many methods to solve this problem, but most of them ignore the special shape characteristics of the dental root, and they are not good at determining the boundary. This paper presents a new method for extracting the root boundary from a cone beam computed tomography image. Firstly, a landmark detection method based on mathematical morphology is established to find the region of interest containing the dental root. Secondly, the image within the region of interest is divided into several levels under the guidance of Hoshen-Kopelman clustering, and the root boundary curve is selected. Polynomial interpolation. Based on the special shape characteristics of the dental root, the root boundary curve is selected by interpolation, and the boundary region is expanded to include the fuzzy boundary region. Finally, the boundary is refined under the guidance of mathematical morphology, and the final boundary is obtained. The effectiveness of the proposed method has been verified by experimental data. An ellipsoid has been cut out as an experiment to prove the accuracy of the method. A comparison of the proposed method with other classical methods has been made, and the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method in extracting the root boundary have been verified. Recent advances in deep learning have enabled us to segment cell and tissue structures in microscopy images. But annotating large-scale image data is time-consuming and costly, and fluorescence microscopy images often have missing or blurred features that can make it difficult to train deep learning models. In this work, we introduce a method to enable uncertainty estimation in deep learning segmentation of fluorescence microscopy images. Our method uses a fully convolutional network with an uncertainty module to predict the segmentation masks and their uncertainties. The uncertainty module takes into account the variability of the predicted values by modeling the posterior distribution via a deep conditional variational network. We show that our method works on a publicly available dataset of fluorescence microscopy images with missing features, and we achieve state-of-the-art results.

The following is a report on an asymptotic expansion of a partition function related to the sinh-function model. This expansion is obtained by the classical method of steepest descent, and it is found that it is in good agreement with the numerical calculation. This paper explores a family of random nobility substitutions, with special emphasis on their properties and applications. The nobility substitutions introduced here are defined by a probability distribution and admit randomness in their values. On the basis of the study of the properties of these random substitutions, we also show the possibility of their application in statistical analysis, optimization, and numerical methods. Through theoretical analysis and numerical simulations, we study the performance and characteristics of the random nobility substitutions in various contexts. In summary, this paper offers an understanding of random nobility substitutions and their practical applications, providing a valuable framework for future research in this area.

In this paper we investigate the relation between non-locality and the geometric structure of dimer algebras. By analyzing different aspects of these notions we try to give a comprehensive picture of their interplay in quantum mechanics. Our results show that the non-locality is closely related to the central properties of dimer algebras, thus suggesting its broader applications for the investigation of quantum systems. Consequently, our study has a further impact on the wider debate about the meaning of non-locality and its role in the formulation of the basic principles of quantum mechanics.

This paper deals with the use of state machines in the design of large scale computer programs and systems. State machines are a powerful tool for modelling and analysing complex systems as they are a clear and concise representation of the system's behaviour. This paper examines the advantages of using state machines in the development of computer programs, namely improved modularity, maintainability, and testability. This paper also describes the various techniques that can be used to construct state machines for large scale systems such as hierarchical state machines and statecharts. Finally, the paper discusses the difficulties and future trends in the use of state machines in the development of large scale computer programs and systems.

In the context of understanding the evolution of galaxies, the universe, and the laws of nature, the ability to model how the intrinsic and extrinsic properties of galaxies produce the observed spectral lines is crucial. The spectral fitting package STECKMAP is designed to fit and simultaneously model the line and continuum spectra of galaxies with complex intrinsic and extrinsic properties. STECKMAP uses the latest models for stellar population synthesis of stellar populations (Marigo et al. 1997), which describe their inner ages, masses, and metallicities. Of particular relevance is the model of galactic star formation (Ivezic et al. 2019), the interstellar medium (ISM; Baumgardt et al. 2017a), and the modeling of the galactic wind and turbulence (Ivezic et al. 2019). AGN (Sulentic & Boroson 2012) can also be taken into account. In this paper, we give a thorough overview of STECKMAP, including the description of the input and the explanation of the fitting procedure. STECKMAP is available as an open-source python extension, and the instructions for installing it are given in the documentation, so we provide here a friendly guide to help users get started with STECKMAP. We strive to make fitting of a galaxy spectrum with STECKMAP an easy and comprehensible experience. Full paper:

Scientific advances in medical images such as MRI have enabled the diagnosis and treatment of a number of diseases. However, medical data are confidential, which imposes a need for reliable and effective image segmentation techniques. In this paper, we propose the framework of BUNET, which uses the architecture of the secure neural network. With BUNET, we combine the confidentiality of blind image segmentation with the accuracy of deep learning, which provides a robust and efficient solution to medical image segmentation. We propose a new, secure artificial intelligence model that performs blind segmentation on encrypted images and that is trained with encrypted images. At the time of training, the encrypted image data are only available to the secure artificial intelligence, and the encrypted image data are not available to the outside world, including the developer and the other people participating in the training. The proposed method is evaluated on a public dataset, and the performance of BUNET is compared with the performance of UNET. The results show that BUNET provides similar performance to UNET with the security and confidentiality of blind image segmentation. Our proposed method can be widely used in various medical image segmentation tasks, especially in the case of medical image confidentiality. BUNET provides a practical and effective solution for secure and confidential medical image segmentation.

It is set in the seventies of the last century, and is founded on the true story of Elizabeth Canning, who, in 1753, was found guilty of perjury. The heroine of the story, who is accused of having murdered her husband, is defended by the learned Sir William Dodd, who determines to prove her innocence. The novel is remarkable for its employment of the detective as a method of finding the truth. The novel was both a critical and popular success, and laid the foundation of the reputation of its author. It has been several times adapted for the stage and for the cinema, and has been subject to a number of critical studies. The Bride of Newgate is regarded as an important step in the evolution of the detective novel, and is said to have influenced writers such as Arthur Conan Doyle and Agatha Christie. Deep learning methods have achieved outstanding results in pixel-level image segmentation. However, they are unable to model the relationship among pixels in medical images due to the limited amount of training data. The ability to effectively use the sparse training data is critical to the success of medical image segmentation. We propose a new method, called a gaussian kernel method, which can use the Gaussian kernel to model the relationship among the neighboring pixels of the specified location (i.e., the query pixel), which significantly improves the performance of supervised segmentation methods and makes it possible to enhance weak supervision segmentation by using only a small fraction of the labeled pixels. In addition, we introduce the concept of patch learning to achieve improved medical image segmentation with sparse labeling. Recent progress in 3D image segmentation relies mostly on the use of either convolutional neural networks or transformer-based models. These two families of models have their limitations: CNNs have a hard time capturing global relationships, and the computationally expensive transformer-based models have difficulty in capturing long-range dependencies, which are common in medical images. We propose a novel framework that combines these two families of models, called CoTr, in an efficient manner. The key idea is hierarchical clustering, a well-known unsupervised learning method, which hierarchically clusters nodes of a graph according to their local similarity. We use this clustering to select the appropriate features from both CNNs and transformers to overcome the limitations of each. On the publicly available monkey dataset with ground truth bounding boxes, our approach achieves a mean accuracy of 92.7 %, which outperforms all other methods tested.

Hierarchical image stripping is a novel approach to image segmentation which employs scale-space filtering techniques. The image is broken down into many layers, each of which represents a different level of abstraction or detail, and each of these layers is then filtered with a series of filters of different scales, which are specifically designed to remove a certain kind of noise or to accentuate certain features. The framework outlined in this paper is sufficiently general to be applicable to many different types of image, including medical, satellite, and natural images, and allows the filters used at each level to be tailored to suit the needs of the application. Hierarchical image stripping is thus a powerful tool for image segmentation which combines the advantages of scale-space filtering with the flexibility of a hierarchical organization.

Abstract: We present a one-shot approach to instantiate unknown objects from a single 2D image into a 3D point cloud. The method combines a neural renderer, a geometrical network, and an optimization procedure. Given an image of a complicated object, our neural renderer is capable of guessing the 3D structure of the object. The geometrical network then refines the initial guess by analyzing the object's shape. Finally, the optimization procedure refines the guess into a convex mesh. We show our approach on a number of diversely complex images, showing that our method is faster and more accurate than the state of the art.

This research is concerned with a multilevel thresholding method which is based on the exploitation of an alternating electric field. Its working principle is that of dividing an image into regions, and applying a series of thresholds to each region. These thresholds are optimised by the alternating electric field so as to minimize the energy required to separate the object from its background. The resulting thresholds are then applied to the entire image so as to produce a binary output. The effectiveness of the method has been proved by experiments and simulations. In all of the tests the results showed that the proposed method surpassed the performance of the most widely used thresholding methods. It also proved to be robust in the presence of noise and differences in illumination. In conclusion this research provides a new and effective method of thresholding images, which exploits the principles of electromagnetism in order to improve its performance and reduce its computational complexity.

We consider the design of convolutional neural networks that are formally hyperbolic. Our construction is based on a recent result in hyperbolic dynamical systems, which states that there is a family of structurally stable, equilibria-preserving, diffeomorphisms that have a finite number of hyperbolic periodic orbits. We use this result to design diffeomorphisms with finite hyperbolic equilibria, and we show that such diffeomorphisms can be used to design formally hyperbolic convolutional neural networks with a formally hyperbolic forward dynamics. We also show that our construction can be used to design convolutional neural networks with a provably hyperbolic backward dynamics, which are necessary to train hyperbolic convolutional neural networks using back-propagation.

We consider the problem of detecting singularities in a sequence of independent observations, in which the singularities are rare events, and the observations are drawn from a known family of distributions. We propose a sequential procedure which is convergent to a theoretical limit as the sample size tends to infinity. We have chosen as our performance measure the total rate of false alarms over the sample period. We take as our driving consideration that the probability of false alarms of any sequential procedure is proportional to the probability of the observations under the null hypothesis, and we wish to minimize this quantity by choosing the test procedure so as to give the smallest possible rate of false alarms over all possible sequences of observations. We prove that the optimum procedure has a simple form and give a closed-form expression for the optimum rate of false alarms. We show that our approach is asymptotically convergent, in the sense that the rate of false alarms is convergent to zero as the sample size tends to infinity, and we give a bound on the convergence rate. Finally, we illustrate the performance of our method with simulated data and compare it with some existing sequential methods.

In this paper we study the relationship between sequential decision problems, dependent types and generic solutions. Sequential decision problems represent a fundamental model for decision making under uncertainty, where a decision maker is faced with a sequence of decisions, each of which is made on the basis of partial information. Dependent types are a logical concept that makes it possible for type systems to reason about the dependencies of values. We show that dependent types can be used to model sequential decision problems in a way that makes it possible to construct generic solutions. We introduce a formalism for encoding sequential decision problems with dependent types, capturing the structure of the problem, that is, the possible actions, states and rewards. We show how dependent types can be used to encode a number of well-known models for sequential decision problems, such as Markov decision processes, partially observable Markov decision processes and reinforcement learning. We develop a generic method for solving sequential decision problems encoded with dependent types. The method is based on backward induction, a well-established method for solving dynamic programs. But in contrast to earlier methods, our method operates directly on the dependent type representation, and can therefore solve complex problems with non-linear interdependencies. We present a number of case studies that demonstrate the usefulness of our method for solving a variety of decision problems from finance, robots and resource allocation. Our results show that dependent types provide a powerful tool for solving sequential decision problems, and that our generic solution is adaptable to a wide variety of problems. We conclude by discussing related work and future directions. We also outline potential applications of our method in artificial intelligence, operations research and type systems. In summary, our paper opens a new perspective on sequential decision making, and demonstrates the power of dependent types for solving complex decision-theoretic problems.
