This paper is concerned with the improvement of image quality in generative adversarial networks (GANs) by ensuring the consistency of the visual appearance of the images they produce. The proposed method uses the normalized Laplacian pyramid distance as a measure of consistency. This measure takes into account the spatial relationships between the image pixels, which means it is more accurate than other distance measures. This method is also computationally cheap and can easily be applied to existing GANs. Experimental results show that the method improves the quality of the images generated.

This study deals with the secure degrees of freedom (DoF) and jammer scaling laws for multi-user wireless networks which exploit opportunistic jammer selection (OJS) technique. This communication system uses the OJS technique to enhance the confidentiality by taking advantage of the multi-user diversity. It begins with the secure DoF, which is characterized by a pre-log of the secrecy capacity. These results show that the secure DoF increases as the number of friendly jammers increases, but it has a finite value because of the limited spatial DoF. Then, it presents a jammer scaling rule that optimizes the secure DoF per jammer. Finally, it provides numerical simulations to prove that the proposed communication system not only significantly increases the secure DoF, but also reduces the complexity of the secret key generation with the increasing number of eavesdroppers. The paper provides a new way for wireless communication systems to increase confidentiality and reduce complexity.

"We discuss a conjecture of Horodecki, Linden, Rhorde and Werner (Phys. Rev. Lett. 2, 547, 1923). That is, they claim that an arbitrary four-particle entangled state has at most one maximally entangled substate. We prove that this conjecture must fail, if one restricts it to states in which each pair of qubits has a positive probability of flipping collectively in the co-ordination basis. An example of such a state is the mixed state frac1d sum_i=1d rho i times rho i*, where rho i and rho i* are maximally entangled states.

The super-pixel method was used to segment and map the eyes of a running rat from several angles. A resolution of 0.01 m was obtained by combining two different methods [1,2]: one with square pixels, the other by superimposing an 88 grid on each pixel in a grayscale image taken at the same depth. Using these two methods, we first computed the 25  26 m grid, varying the distances between each eye and in the middle between the pupil and the iris, to produce a virtual field of view of 40 °. After projecting the image in the usual pixel projection, we applied a calibration procedure to obtain a reduction of the a priori height of the background as black. Then we used super-pixel superpositions with twelve superimposed images of different parts of the visual space of the subject, corresponding to the different angles of vision. These super-pixel superpositions resulted in a 2 2 superposition of the four 4-by 4-m binarized frames of the images. We could achieve a 3D resolution of up to 0.01 m, corresponding to a field of view of about 170 ° according to the usual views on the vision of mammals (a field of view 50–100 ° broader than the field of view of the current stereo methods). This resolution shows that the super-pixels or their analogs would not be needed to represent the high-frequency information. In order to obtain a higher resolution at lower intensities, the images used here were deliberately a little diffraction. This contrasts with the method described in other works on the same subject. We are here interested only in a better representation of the details without loss of sharpness and, therefore, less complex systems. Moreover, the more information we have, the more objects we see, even if they are low frequency. The current implementation is a test for the generalization to higher resolutions.

This paper proposes a method for estimating the aleatory uncertainty of medical images with convolutional neural networks and test-time augmentation. The aleatory uncertainty is the natural variability of data that may influence the accuracy of the image processing. Test-time augmentation is a method of generating a large number of augmented images while learning, which can be used to represent this variability. The proposed method combines the test-time augmentation with the convolutional neural network-based segmentation model to estimate the aleatory uncertainty. Experiments on a medical image dataset show that the proposed method increases the accuracy of the segmentation and provides reliable uncertainty estimates. The proposed method is expected to improve the reliability and interpretability of medical image segmentation models.

TransBTS is a new approach for multimodal brain tumor segmentation based on the transformer network architecture. It combines multiple imaging modalities, such as T1, T2, and fluid-attenuated inversion-recovery (FLAIR) images, to obtain more accurate and robust segmentation results. It uses a hybrid loss function that combines the Dice loss and the cross-entropy loss, to optimize the performance of segmentation. Experimental results on two publicly available datasets, BraTS2019 and BraTS2020, show that TransBTS outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. This suggests a potential for clinical application.

Rowmotion is a concept of group theory. It is used to study automorphisms of groups. In this paper we generalize the concept of rowmotion to the generalized group of automorphisms and we study the properties of the rowmotion of a generalized group. We also prove some important results on the relation between rowmotion and generalized groups. At the end of the paper we formulate some open problems and issues for further research.

In this paper we propose a novel self-trained learning method called Prior-Guided Local Self-Trained Learning (PGL) for the task of 3D medical image segmentation. Our method uses the power of prior knowledge and local information to improve the accuracy and robustness of self-trained learning for medical image segmentation. As compared with previous work, our method can learn from a relatively small set of annotated images, resulting in more efficient and scalable learning. Our method consists of two main components: a prior knowledge and self-trained learning module, which can learn domain-specific knowledge. Our method is evaluated on three publicly available datasets, including brain tumor, liver and lung. Our experimental results show that PGL can outperform state-of-the-art self-trained learning methods on both accuracy and robustness. Furthermore, we conduct an ablation study to evaluate the effectiveness of different components of our method, demonstrating the effectiveness of the use of prior knowledge and local information in improving the performance of self-trained learning. Our work is useful for the task of medical image segmentation, especially for tasks where annotated images are sparse. PGL can use the power of prior knowledge and local information to improve the accuracy and robustness of segmentation for a variety of medical applications.

The architecture of RatLesNetv2 is based on the U-Net architecture. The encoder part of the network is composed of five convolutional layers and two pooling layers, and the decoder part is composed of four convolutional layers and two up-convolutional layers. The final result of the network is a 11 convolutional layer. We have evaluated the performance of RatLesNetv2 on a publicly available T2 MR rat lesion image set, DMRI-RL, with 131 images, and the results of the experiment indicate that the segmentation of RatLesNetv2 is superior to previous lesion segmentation methods with an average Dice score of 0.874.

Recent years have witnessed a remarkable improvement in the efficiency of image-processing methods, as a result of the greater availability of large annotated and unannotated datasets and the greater ability of deep-learning-based models to capture image-dependent dependencies. Most of these methods have tended to focus on modeling local dependencies and have neglected the context of the image, which often carries information that helps to clarify local image areas. Some methods have been able to generate pixel-level annotations that can be used as input to the segmentation models, thus avoiding the need for semantic annotations. However, these methods cannot take advantage of unlabeled data, which limits their effectiveness. In this paper, we use global and local mutual information to regularize a convolutional encoder, a conditional random field (CRF)-based model, and a pixel-level classifier (i.e., a discriminative CRF). They are all applied to the output of the respective models, which then guide their predictions. We have evaluated our proposed method on publicly available data and we see significant improvements over existing methods in terms of accuracy. We show that although the regularizers should be carefully tuned to obtain the best results, they have proven quite useful for a variety of tasks and data. The interstellar medium, which plays an important role in the formation of galaxies, alters their spectra by reflection, absorption, and re-emission. A correct modelling of this influence is necessary to a correct understanding of the evolution and structure of galaxies. In this paper, we propose a new method of modelling galaxy spectra in the presence of interstellar dust, applicable to nearby and distant galaxies. We combine the best available dust models with a range of stellar atmospheres, to provide both stellar and interstellar properties. We apply this method to a set of observed spectra and test it by comparison with existing models and new observational data. We also explore the relation between extinction and optical depth, and consider the implication of our results for the study of extragalactic dust distributions. Our method provides a powerful new tool for the study of the complex relations between dust and stars in galaxies, and promises to significantly advance our understanding of the evolution and structure of galaxy populations.

This paper treats of a problem of non-adaptive, and simultaneous, test on a graph. A certain number of vertices are chosen to be tested, and it is proposed to detect, with the least number of operations, those which have the property to be tested for. We have proposed a new method of attacking this problem by a combination of spectral and combinatorial methods, namely, spectral clustering. Our method is based on the following idea. If a cluster contains a vertex which has the property to be tested for, then it is probable that many of its neighbors have it also. Therefore, by testing each cluster in detail, it is possible to detect the clusters containing the vertices with the property quickly, thereby reducing the number of tests. We have theoretically analyzed the performance of this method and have proved that it is very nearly the best between the number of tests and the probability of finding the vertices which have the property. We have also experimented with it on real graphs and have verified that it scales well for large graphs. Hence, our method is very powerful in a non-adaptive simultaneous test on a graph. It also shows the efficacy of a combination of spectral methods and combinatorial methods for the solution of difficult optimization problems.

In the following article, we introduce a new image segmentation technique combining the concept of a geodesic with the enhancement of an implicit region of the homogeneity of the image. The proposed method is intended to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the image segmentation, using geometric and structural information in the image. The geodesic paths between the pixels are then used to group them into homogeneous regions, thus improving the implicit homogeneity of the image. The basis of the proposed method is the observation that images can be represented as a graph, where pixels are nodes and the similarity between them is defined by the weighted degree of the edges. By calculating the geodesic paths between the pixels, we can reveal the underlying graph structure of the image and thus identify the regions of homogeneous characteristics. We test our method on several standard images and compare the results with other standard image segmentation methods. Our results show that our method outperforms traditional image segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and speed. The main contributions of this article are as follows: We introduce a new image segmentation method that combines the concept of a geodesic with the enhancement of the implicit homogeneity of the image. We introduce a new method of calculating the geodesic paths between the pixels, taking into account the similarity of their characteristics. We show that our method is effective on several standard images, and outperforms standard methods in terms of both accuracy and speed. The article is structured as follows: in the second section, we briefly review the previous work on image segmentation and geodesics. In the third section, we describe the proposed method in more detail. In the fourth section, we report our results and discuss them. In the fifth section, we conclude the article, discussing future work and directions for further research. The proposed method can be used for a wide range of applications, such as object recognition, tracking and scene understanding. The question of the minimum number of bidders required for a truthful auction of a commodity which is known to be influenced by secondary information is examined. We take into account that each buyer may have a private value of the good, but a secondary value may also be available to modify it. It is shown that the secondary information has the power to reduce the complexity of the auction in terms of the number of buyers required, in comparison with a situation in which it is not available. This results in the theoretical explanation of the role of secondary information in auction design, and in the practical direction of auctions in which secondary information is present.

In feudal Japan, a young warrior named Hiroshi avenges his father's death at the hands of the warlord Katsumoto. He goes to Katsumoto's castle and challenges him to a duel for the samurai sword. In the middle of this journey, he encounters many dangers and difficulties, and he is forced to make many decisions, and he has to face many struggles. He meets an old samurai who teaches him the way of the samurai, and a beautiful young girl named Yumi who has captured his heart. As the day of the duel approaches, Hiroshi has to confront his past, face his fears, and decide whether the desire for revenge is worth sacrificing his conscience. Finally, in the final, magnificent duel for the samurai sword, he shows his courage and conviction to the limit.

The purpose of this study was to develop a fuzzy clustering-based segmentation method to segment vertebrae from T1-weighted spinal MR images. The proposed method begins with preprocessing the MR images to enhance the contrast and remove the noise. It is then applied the fuzzy clustering to group similar pixels into vertebrae. The clusters are refined with morphological operations to improve the accuracy and reduce the false positives. The experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a high accuracy and speed in recognizing the vertebrae in T1-weighted spinal MR images, with an average precision of 96% and recall of 98%. Compared with the conventional thresholding method, the proposed method had a high sensitivity and lower false positives. Moreover, the recognition of the vertebrae from spinal MR images by the fuzzy clustering-based method provides useful information for clinical diagnosis and treatment planning.

This paper presents a novel decomposition for discriminative image segmentation with super-modularity. Discriminative segmentation aims to detect objects in an image and to predict their classes. Super-modularity is a loss function that encourages the model to create a correct and consistent object boundary. However, a super-modular loss function is computationally expensive to optimize, so the decomposition framework addresses this issue by decomposing the segmentation problem into two sub-problems: the first is the task of predicting a set of non-overlapping regions of interest in the image, and the second is the classification task of predicting the class label of each region. The first task is formulated as a super-modular problem, which can be efficiently solved by a graph-based method. The second task is formulated as a standard classification task that can be solved using a common classification method. The decomposition framework has several advantages over the existing discriminative methods. First, it can efficiently optimize super-modularity, which will enhance the accuracy of the results. Second, it can use standard classification methods, which simplifies the training process and improves the efficiency of the model. Finally, it can use knowledge about the image to make the model more robust and interpretable. We test the framework on several standard image datasets and show that it outperforms existing discriminative methods. We also conduct an ablation study to verify the efficiency of the decomposition framework and show that it improves the accuracy and efficiency of the model. This paper makes an important contribution to the field of discriminative image segmentation by proposing an efficient decomposition framework for super-modularity. The proposed framework has a wide range of applications in the field of computer vision, including object detection, semantic segmentation, and image segmentation.

In this paper, we study axiom-A polynomial skew-products of C2 and their postcritical sets. We give a homoclinic characterisation of the postcritical set of axiom-A skew-products and give examples of such skew-products. We also prove that any axiom-A skew-product has a dense invariant Cantori set which is homeomorphic to the solenoidal skew-product. We study the dynamics of these Cantori sets and compare it with the dynamics of the original axiom-A skew-product. Finally, we discuss the existence of the Fatou–Bieberbach domain for axiom-A skew-products. We conclude that our results give a complete understanding of axiom-A skew-products and their postcritical sets.

The problem of fault detection in three-dimensional seismic images is a crucial problem for many industrial applications. However, the annotation of these images with fault lables is an expensive operation that affects the efficiency of fault segmentation. In this paper, we present an attention-based 3D fault segmentation method that labels faults with high accuracy using very few fault lables in two dimensions. We show that the learning process only needs a few fault labels to identify faults in the three-dimensional space. We tested our method on several benchmarks and showed that our method outperforms many state-of-the-art methods with very few fault lables in two dimensions. Our method can greatly reduce the time and resources required for fault segmentation and therefore revolutionize the seismological exploration industry.

The reaction cross-section and angular distribution of Ne-12,23+ (p,n) at energies relevant to astrophysical studies is reported. “A woman—Dana, the character played by Meg Ryan—was raped and murdered and her body was found floating in Long Island Sound, six months before the film begins. A husband and wife, friends of the murdered woman, Ben and Claire, seek to find the culprit without assistance or information from the police. They didn’t leave her alone, and she fought off one while Ben ran after the other to stop him. But it was too late, someone murdered Dana before they could find the guilty party.”

This paper proposes a novel approach to document image segmentation using a fast, fully-connected convolutional neural network. The conventional fully-connected convolutional neural networks are very time-consuming, and their applicability to practical tasks is limited by their high complexity. Our proposed method makes use of the concept of octave convolutions, which offer speedups and reduced memory consumption compared to conventional convolutions. By combining this technique with a carefully designed architecture and a careful tunable optimization strategy, we obtain state-of-the-art performance on several reference datasets. Our method achieves a very high F1-score of 96.5% on the commonly used DIVA-HisDB dataset, while being noticeably faster than existing methods. In sum, the main contributions of this paper are: - We propose a fast, fully-connected, octave convolutional neural network (CNN) for document image segmentation, which can achieve high performance while reducing its complexity. - We design a new architecture and a tuning strategy tailored to the document image segmentation task, which leads to improved performance and efficiency. Extensive experiments have been conducted, and it has been demonstrated that our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. This work has important implications for various applications, such as document scanning, optical character recognition (OCR), and the digitalization of historical archives. The proposed method has the potential to allow real-time document image analysis and processing, which could help improve the efficiency and productivity of industry.

This paper deals with the structure of lines in three dimensions, and proves some new theorems of a type which may be applied to the lines in three dimensions. We begin by extending the classical theorem of Pythagorem to higher dimensions; and then we examine the finite version of the problem, and answer questions as to the number of lines necessary for the existence of the necessary monochromatic groups. The application of these results to various fields, such as physics and engineering, is also considered. Our work is a step forward in the understanding of the concept of a line in three dimensions.

This paper treats of a maximal abelian subalgebra and a projection in two Banach algebras associated with a topological dynamical system. In the first part we define these notions and give some basic properties. In the second part we prove that every maximal abelian subalgebra is contained in a projection subspace. Then we prove that if a projection subspace contains a maximal abelian subalgebra, it is a projection. Finally we give an example.

Something Rotten is the story of a hardworking journalist, John, who has landed his dream job with a prestigious newspaper, only to discover that his boss, Walter, is a rotten and corrupt man who will do anything to hold on to his power and wealth. As John finds more and more evidence of Walter’s illegal activities, he is threatened and has to decide whether to stay quiet or to risk everything to uncover the truth. Alongside the main storyline, there are other characters such as Emily, an intern from Stanford University, who is underestimated by everyone but turns out to be a very helpful aid to John’s investigations, and Dave, John’s childhood friend, who is always ready to give John wise advice. The reader is taken on a suspenseful roller-coaster ride, through plot twists and turns, which exposes how far people are prepared to go for their own benefit, and how they react when one person decides that enough is enough.

Ternaus-Net, a neural network based on the U-net architecture, employs a pre-trained VGG11 encoder from the ImageNet dataset. Ternaus-Net shows improved performance compared to traditional U-net models.

These axioms are formulated in the most general way possible, without referring to any specific physical system. They are then used to derive Newton's dynamic laws, including the laws of motion, the law of universal gravitation, and the law of inertia. The system outlined in this paper is different from the traditional approach to Newtonian mechanics, which is based on the laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation. The approach outlined in this paper is based on the assumption that the laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation are not true, and the axioms are then used to derive the laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation. On the island of Mount Sinabung, a mighty warrior by the name of Wiro Sableng—known for his ability to cut off five heads at a time—falls in love with the beautiful Princess Malin Kundang. It is written that whoever enters the royal palace through its main gate shall be sure to die. But on the way back to their homeland, they take two different paths, reunite in Yogyakarta, and then once more, to protect themselves from danger, she changes her name to Putri Ngertjahi and becomes a servant in Tengenan, near Mount Kawi, to avoid danger, as the conflict has now become an all-out war. At this time, Jago Dalih and Ronggo Ngetod come to her palace under the names of Aman Ranting and Cempaka Ligur, disguised as men who are ready to fight Prince Bima Indrajaya, who is their enemy. In Chicago in 1892, Mamah Borthwick-Cheek, née Cassatt, had just given birth to her second child, when a new family arrived in the neighborhood: Frank Lloyd Wright and his pregnant wife, Kitty Lloyd-Jones. She had just turned twenty-five, twelve years older than Frank’s first-born, John, then thirteen. She invited both families to a social evening and friendship was instantaneous. During that summer, all of them went on vacation to Waukegan, where Frank set up his studio in Mamah’s house while she was nursing little Kate, who was not very well. He offered it as a gift to Mamah, with the proviso that it should be used by any of the male members of the family. By the end of the following summer, Frank had finished his design for a house for Mamah’s husband, Edwin Chee, named Taliesin, in honor of the ancient bard of Wales whose work he was often inspired by. Now, at the end of December 1895, he was already having an affair with Mamah and also getting to know her daughter Marian, whom she brought to the house at holiday times. One night, Mamah told everyone goodnight except Frank. Early in March, they travelled to Milwaukee together and then returned to Oak Park because Frank had come down with pneumonia at Taliesin. During June or July, they decided to leave Illinois for good, partly because Frank wanted more freedom from the gossip about his adultery, in the midst of a society that was in awe of him and his work, and in awe of the woman who could love an architect as no one else.

This paper proposes a new method of image extraction based on fuzzy rule based design. It makes full use of the advantages of fuzzy reasoning and rule-based systems to extract images from complex backgrounds with irregular shapes and ambiguous boundaries. Then it introduces the concept of fuzzy rule based on image features and its application in improving the extraction accuracy and efficiency. The proposed method consists of three steps: first, image features are extracted, such as colors, textures, edges, etc., from the image; second, the extracted features are converted into fuzzy numbers to deal with uncertainties and imprecision; third, fuzzy rules are established to divide the image into objects. These rules are based on the language variables, and they are flexible and adaptable to different images. The feasibility of the method is verified by experiments on images of different complexity. Compared with the existing methods, the fuzzy rules based on image features have higher extraction accuracy, shorter extraction time, and higher robustness to noise and other factors. This paper makes a great contribution to the field of image processing, providing a new way of dealing with the difficulties of image extraction by combining fuzzy reasoning and rule-based design. In terms of applications, it has an important reference significance for object recognition, medical image and robot vision, etc., and has broad application prospects.

Feeling trapped and stifled, she begins a personal journey of discovery, finding new creativity, re-establishing old friendships and searching for a new meaning. Title: Expansions of differential Lie algebras. Abstract: We study extensions of Lie algebras associated with differential operators acting on the complex numbers. Our main result gives a characterization of solvable extensions in terms of commuting differential operators and estimates their dimension. We give examples of such extensions and discuss some of their applications to the study of analytic functions. In particular, we prove that all solvable Lie algebras generated by differential operators are free algebras. This is a new proof of a classical result of Levi.

This paper deals with the problem of direction-of-arrival estimation in the presence of subspace leakage, which arises when the main signal is contaminated by impure signals. Subspace leakage seriously degrades the performance of the polarization estimation methods, especially in small sample cases. To solve this problem, we propose a new method called subspace leakage analysis and improved direction-of-arrival estimation (SLAIDE). SLAIDE consists of two steps: (1) subspace leakage analysis to identify the existence and degree of subspace leakage; and (2) improved direction-of-arrival estimation, which uses the result of subspace leakage analysis to improve the estimation accuracy. The performance of SLAIDE is evaluated by using both simulation and real data. It is shown that SLAIDE has a much higher accuracy than existing methods, especially in small sample cases, and is robust to various types of subspace leakage. The main contributions of this paper are as follows. A new approach for analyzing subspace leakage and improved direction-of-arrival estimation. A detailed study of the proposed method by using both simulation and real data. A summary of the results and a discussion of the results.

We present an unsupervised semi-supervised learning method for the segmentation of histological images, whose labelled training examples are rare, and many available but unannotated histological images are available. The proposed method is two-step: first, it learns how to classify each patch of histological images using the context information of their surroundings, and it is self-supervised with large or even all the combinations of the unannotated areas and their associated labels, which are inferred from the spatial relationships among them in a single histological slide. It is the aim of this paper to present a novel method of semi-supervised segmentation that ensures consistency in hard regions. Hard regions are regions which are difficult to identify because of their noise, heterogeneity, and blurred boundaries, and these characteristics have largely affected the performance of conventional methods of image segmentation. We propose a strategy for identifying these regions iteratively and imposing consistency on them using a new loss function. It has been shown in experiments on several medical image datasets that the proposed method gives a marked improvement in accuracy and robustness to noise. A detailed analysis of the impact of consistency on the learning process is also presented. Our study suggests that the idea of ensuring consistency in hard regions could be a promising way of improving performance in semi-supervised medical image segmentation.

It is proved that the Fisher Information is approximately equal to the log-likelihood Hessian in the high-dimensional case, and that the Cramer-Rao bound is close in the high-dimensional case. It is shown that the Fisher Information is approximated by the log-likelihood Hessian in the high-dimensional case, and that the Cramer-Rao bound is tight. A simple algorithm for the computation of the Fisher Information and the Cramer-Rao bound is outlined, and its performance is tested on simulated and real data.

Three-fluid dynamical model and experimental data. The 3-fluid dynamical model has been employed in predicting the diffusion coefficient of water molecules in the brain, which may serve as a measure of neuronal activity. In this work we compared the diffusion coefficient predicted by the 3-fluid dynamical model with the diffusion coefficient measured by diffusion tensor imagining (DTI), which shows the path of water molecules in the brain. The DTI results were superior to the DTI predictions. However, the DTI gave a higher diffusion coefficient for water molecules in the brain than did the 3-fluid dynamical model, and so the 3-fluid dynamical model may be a useful method for predicting the dynamics of the brain.

Ultrasound contrast agents (UCAs) are microbubbles (MBs) which are injected intravenously to enhance the visualization of blood vessels. They may also be used in therapeutics, opening the blood–brain barrier, and gene and drug delivery. The mechanical response of MBs to ultrasound is complex and is not well understood. In this paper we present a macroscopic analogy for the mechanical response of a MB to an incident ultrasound wave. The analogy is based on a gas-filled elastomer membrane, the pressure inside the membrane replacing the surface tension. We use the analogy to study the response of a MB to an incident wave and compare the results with a 2D simulation. We find good agreement between the two, indicating that the analogy is a useful tool for the study of the mechanical response of MBs to ultrasound.

This model is capable of rich phase-transitions, including antiferromagnetism, dimerization, and a new columnar phase with the underlying bond-order wave. We concentrate on the paramagnetic region of the phase diagram and determine the critical lines between the paramagnetic and other phases, with the exception of the columnar phase. These phases are then analyzed by the finite-size scaling method. The paramagnetic phase is found to be essentially cubic, and the paramagnetic-to-antiferromagnetic transition can be well described by the three-dimensional Ising model. Moreover, we find a finite-size effect in the dimer phase, which suggests the existence of a first-order phase transition between the paramagnetic and dimer phases. This study contributes to the understanding of the influence of the spin and the lattice on the phase diagram and critical behavior of the BEG model.

The emergence of diversity in machine learning challenges current learning theories and may provide opportunities to improve the performance of training neural networks and general AI applications. In this paper we report experiments using diversity to enhance generalization during the initial stage of learning character recognition that reveals a surprising trade-off between locality and diversity in the context of the data structure. We show that at high levels of diversity (k=1) accuracy is comparable to that obtained by choosing higher level local maxima (in both cases). At low levels of diversity (k=0), however, locality does not appear to be detrimental. Future study of learning with multiple levels of diversity will permit better characterization of its effects not only on accuracy, but also on generalizability and robustness. Result: At low levels of diversity, greater accuracy is obtained than at high levels. When ten diverse values are introduced, an ensemble of three models performs 0.8% worse than any other group despite having a similar distribution. Similarly, the accuracy of an ensemble of three models that assigns a different value to each of the 30 training examples is two times that of the original method, and the diversity of the models is almost perfectly balanced. These results strongly suggest that high levels of diversity are superior for learning to recognize a class, or a general purpose inference, both supervised and unsupervised, and that these characteristics may be important for learning efficiency. We note that in this experiment the sample size was very small, and the asymmetry of the learning may lead to an underestimate of the efficiency. Secondly, although the learning would be more precise with higher level local minima, it is possible that there may be diminishing returns because of the increased variability at the local minima. Lastly, we need to consider further evidence, for example lower bounds obtained by different methods.

We study the structure of finite-dimensional real and complex Lie algebras which are nearly abelian, in particular those with a small commutator subalgebra and/or nilradical. We obtain new results on the structure of solvable Lie algebras and generalize some results of the classical Engel theorem. The main tool we employ is the algebraic version of the Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff formula due to Kostrikin and Shafarevich.

The Brooklyn Follies is a novel by Paul Auster, published in 2005, and is the third installment of his New York Trilogy, after The New York Trilogy and Moon Palace. It is set in the early 1980s, and revolves around the lives of a group of characters in Brooklyn, New York. The novel is non-linear, with the storyline jumping back and forth in time, and with different characters providing the narrator’s point of view. The novel begins with the story of a young man, Daniel Quinn, who works as a security guard in a museum in Brooklyn. One night, a man named Max asks him to help him steal a painting from the museum. Daniel is reluctant at first, but eventually agrees to help Max, and the two men plan a theft. They succeed in stealing the painting, but Daniel is caught by the security cameras, and is dismissed from his job. Then the novel shifts to the story of Max, a wealthy art dealer, who is married to a woman named Lydia, and has a young son, Sam. He also has an affair with Nina, a painter. Nina is married to a writer named Peter, and they are friends. Peter and Max often help each other with their writing. Nina struggles with her marriage and her relationship with Max. She also struggles with her art, and becomes disillusioned with it, so she begins an affair with a musician named David, who is married to a dancer named Sarah. Sarah and Nina become friends, and Nina begins to help Sarah with her art. Then the novel shifts to the story of Sarah, who is also struggling with her marriage and relationship with David, as well as her career as a dancer. She begins an affair with a painter named Paul, who is married to a writer named Susan. They become friends, and Susan begins to help Sarah with her dancing. Then the novel shifts to the story of Susan, who is struggling with her marriage and her relationship with Paul. She also struggles with her writing.

Yet, in spite of their potential advantages, a thorough study of the problem of bringing the source-segmentation to a target locality is as yet a scarce one in the literature on medical image analysis. We consider such adaptation to be essential in clinical conditions where data-sets of a given clinical nature are rare and the clinical anatomies vary considerably from one center to another. In the present paper we address the problem of adapting a source-segmentation model for the detection of mitotic cells in breast histology images to a target institution, with only a small number of images from the target institution already annotated. We propose a simple yet effective framework for domain adaptation, based on a combination of global and local adaptation. The former relies on a global adaptation which conditions the source-segmentation on the batch normalization statistics from the target site; the latter relies on a local adaptation which, for the very few target-images that have been annotated, allows for a further fine-tuning of the source-segmentation on a few of the target images. We have evaluated our method on a new data-set, and we have obtained significantly better results than those obtained with the source-segmentation unadjusted, and on those obtained with a method which is initialized directly from the target-images.

The story of a group of scientists and scientists exhibiting the evidence of evolution. The exhibition, entitled the Greatest Show on Earth, takes visitors on a trip through time, space, and species and reveals the fascinating history of life on earth. The visitors learn about the fossil record, comparative anatomy, and molecular biology and how these sciences prove the fact of evolution. The exhibition is filled with engaging, interactive features and reveals the science in a fun and entertaining way for all ages. Visitors are forced to examine their own assumptions about the natural world. Some struggle to reconcile their religious beliefs with scientific evidence, while others are inspired to learn more about the wonders of the natural world. At the same time, a group of anti-evolutionists, led by a charismatic and well-funded leader, launches a campaign to denigrate the exhibition and offer an alternative explanation for the diversity of life on earth. While the conflict between science and pseudo-science escalates, the team behind the exhibition must defend their work and the scientific method. The reader is given a unique view of the preparation of the exhibition, from the first meeting to the first copy. The Greatest Show on Earth ends up bringing science, enlightenment, and ultimately, acceptance to millions of visitors.

A witness structure is a special kind of combinatorial structure which is associated with a polynomial map and which carries with it a variety of information on the roots of the polynomial. In the present work we will employ witness structures to construct a new family of complexes, which have topological significance, and are associated with systems of polynomial equations, and which carry with them the topological information of these systems of equations analogously to the algebraic information of the witness structures. We will show that these complexes are homotopical to a certain kind of complex involving the WITner spectra. This fact will allow us to determine the homotopical type of the complex associated with a system of equations by a study of the roots of the polynomials in question.

In this paper, we present a new approach to the interpretation of modal logics, which we call a modal-functional interpretation. This interpretation combines the advantages of the previously known modal-functional interpretations, while avoiding their shortcomings. In the usual modal-functional interpretation, possibilities are taken to be possible worlds and necessity as membership in these possible worlds. These interpretations have difficulty in representing deontic concepts such as obligation and permission. Dialectical interpretations take possibilities as being a state of an agent's attitudes towards the world, but they are unable to represent systematically the relationship between these attitudes. Our new modal-functional interpretation, the modal-functional interpretation (the dialectical interpretation), avoids these difficulties by assuming that possibilities are functions of agent-centered perspectives of truth values. These functions can be combined using standard logical operations, which makes it possible to systematically express complex modal concepts. We also introduce a semantics for this system, which makes it possible to distinguish the subtleties of the belief and commitment of an agent from a situation. We demonstrate the versatility of this approach by applying it to several problems in epistemology, temporal modalities and deontic systems. We discuss the unexpected connections between these three areas, and show how the modal-functional interpretation (the dialectical interpretation) provides a unified framework for long-standing problems. We discuss the significance of this work for current debates in philosophy, artificial intelligence and psychology. We argue that the modal-functional interpretation (the dialectical interpretation) is a promising starting point for further research on the nature of modality and the role of modality in human reasoning and decision-making.

This paper proposes a new method of model selection for time series forecasting, a graphical lasso. The method is based on the fact that the regression coefficients are gradually shrunk to zero by means of a regularization operator with an L1 constraint. The regularization coefficient is determined graphically, which gives the opportunity for visual interpretation of the selection process. The method is applied to time series data and tested by means of simulation and on real data. The results show that the method outperforms the conventional methods both in terms of forecast accuracy and time-consuming computation. Moreover, it gives more interpretable results, as the graphic representation of the regularization coefficient allows identifying the most important predictors for forecasting. The paper ends with a discussion of the application of the method to a large number of time series data and its potential for future research.

This article deals with the change of charge in an electrically charged, non-rotating black hole known as the Schwarzchild black hole. It tries to explain how this change is due to external factors such as temperature or gravitational force on nearby matter. Our results indicate that the resulting variability is not well understood by the framework of general relativity alone. But if we include quantum mechanics, we may be able to gain a better understanding of the behavior of the electric charge in regions of spacetime with a strong curvature, such as those around massive bodies, including supermassive bodies in the centers of galaxies, which also have these properties, and so this study is of interest not only for academics, but for practical applications as well, especially when considering the possible observational signals that could be obtained with telescopes studying distant astrophysical phenomena in strong gravitation fields where effects could become noticeable if further research were conducted.

Intro: In recent years, the study of non-orientable Lagrangians and their geometry has developed considerably, and new mathematical structures have been constructed to analyze these Lagrangians. In this paper, the recent developments of the study of A* algebras for non-orientable Lagrangians are reviewed. This paper provides a suitable framework for the study of these Lagrangians. In order to understand the characteristics of the non-orientable Lagrangians, it is necessary to construct a rich algebraic structure that includes the symmetries of the Lagrangian. A* algebras have proven to be useful for this purpose. They can naturally model the symmetries of the Lagrangian.. For example, it was observed that equivariant A* algebras were obtained by identifying different branches of the same Lagrangian. The equivariant A* algebras were used to identify different branches of the Lagrangian. The main result of this paper is the construction of equivariant A* algebras for non-orientable Lagrangians by identifying different branches of the Lagrangian by symmetry transformations. The equivariant A* algebras are defined by the Maurer-Cartan elements satisfying some conditions related to the symmetry transformations. Several examples of the non-orientable Lagrangians that can be analyzed using this framework are presented. The framework constructed in this paper provides a natural way of modelling the symmetries of the Lagrangian and identifying different branches of the Lagrangian.

Introduction. The most common explanation of the formation of galaxies is that they grow by the accretion of smaller galaxies. It is based on the fact that most dark matter halos are the result of the merging of smaller halos, and galaxies in these halos evolve by dissipative structures, where the gas is collected from the medium of hydrogen. At lower mass scales, one can expect the formation of the galaxy to be dominated more by the action of gravity and dissipative movement. This is the most likely way to create a strong star formation. Studies of nearby merged, interacting and starburst galaxies have shown that they have a higher star formation rate than non-interacting galaxies (eg Surace, 2004; Kennicutt, 1992). It has long been assumed that the galaxies forming stars most frequently are those of low mass and high metallicity at high redshift (eg Cowie et al., 1996), which has been confirmed by a number of studies (see the discussion of Moustakas in 2006). ). It is also well known that the rate of star formation increases with the redshift (Lilly et al., 1997). The star formation in the low-mass galaxies (M_B = 14.5, M_B = 3  107 M) found by Bouwens et al. (2004, 2006) at z  7 has been found to be comparable to that in the more massive galaxies (M_B  21, M_B  3  1011 M) at z  1 (Bouwens et al., 2003). While Bouwens et al. (2007, Bouwens et al., 2006) argued strongly for an increase in the density of star formation at z > 5 (with a peak in star formation at z  6.5), the HUDF (eg Bouwens et al., 2006) sample is based on a rare sample of galaxies, and does not represent typical starburst galaxies. At z = 0, the rate of star formation in galaxies follows the same relations as in the galaxies of lower redshift: the more metals there are, the higher the star formation rate. That is, the starburst galaxies have the highest metallicity and the highest star formation rate. The highest star formation in starburst galaxies, which are galaxies of the lower masses, at the higher metallicities, is mainly caused by the activity of internal shock waves and turbulent motions.

In the suburban sprawl of Detroit, thirteen-year-old Connor and his younger brother Patrick struggle to survive on their own after their mother’s death, living in constant fear of being found by Child Protective Services or, worse still, by one of the vicious gangs that roam the streets. But when they stumble on an abandoned mansion full of strange artifacts, unusual creatures, and dangerous secrets, things take a sinister turn, and they discover that Detroit is home to two warring factions fighting for control of a potent magic that could give immortality but also destroy the world, the “Great Disruption.” They will need all their cunning and resourcefulness and learn to trust each other, as well as learn to rely on friendships formed with the most unlikely allies. In this first installment of a trilogy, Monster Blood, Tattoo, finds Connor and Patrick on an odyssey full of wonder, danger, discovery, redemption, love, loss, and adventure.

Interest in connectomics has been growing rapidly in recent years. A thorough understanding of the brain requires an accurate reconstruction of neural connections and identification of the synaptic connections between neurons. Although many methods have been proposed for predicting the synaptic connections, there is still a need to improve their accuracy and speed. In this study, we propose a fully automatic method for predicting and verifying synaptic connections in EM images. The method is based on a deep learning method, using a convolutional neural network (CNN) to predict synaptic connections from raw EM images. We trained and tested our method on a large set of more than 1000 EM images. Our method achieved high accuracy, precision, and recall for all images with only a 0.05 false positive rate. In addition, we verified the putative synaptic connections predicted by other methods with high accuracy.

During his childhood in the land of the dragons, young Arin had never dreamed of being a hero who could fight dragons and protect people. We introduce an improved version of an efficient Vertex Cover Problem for graphs of bounded treewidth. Our reduced problem is to find a minimum-weight subgraph covering all vertices and containing no P3 subgraph. We show that the vertex cover problem on graphs of bounded treewidth can be solved in O(k2n), where n is the number of vertices. This improves the previous best-known bound of O(k3n).

This paper presents a novel approach to learning pose variation in a shape population by combining a set of shape examples with varying poses. This is done by modelling the variance of the poses with factor analysis, while imposing constraints on the factor structure to guarantee consistency between the example poses. Experimental results on datasets of human faces and 3D objects show that the proposed method is successful in handling pose variation and improves the accuracy of shape classification.

Vision transformers (ViTs) have recently emerged as a powerful approach for image classification. However, it is not easy to train ViTs effectively, since the choice of training data, data augmentation and regularization methods must be carefully considered. In this paper, we investigate the effect of various data strategies, data augmentation and regularization methods on the performance of ViTs. We conduct extensive experiments on a number of image classification tasks and analyze the results to find the best conditions for training ViTs. We show that large datasets are more effective, as are diverse augmentation methods and regularization methods such as dropout and weight decay. We also propose a new regularization method, patch-level dropout, which can help improve the performance of ViTs by encouraging the model to pay attention to different parts of images. Our results provide a useful guide to the training of ViTs and shed light on the factors that contribute to the success of ViTs in image classification tasks.

This paper deals with the Milnor number of a singularity on a hyper-surface in arbitrary characteristic. The Milnor number is a fundamental measure of the complexity of a singularity. The authors develop a new formula for the Milnor number, in terms of the local cohomology of the singularity. They also study the behaviour of the Milnor number under deformation and resolution of the singularity. The results have a bearing on the understanding of the structure and properties of hyper-surface singularities, and they could have applications in algebraic geometry and singularity theory.

Image segmentation is an important task in image processing and machine learning, and it involves dividing the image into several regions, each of which represents a different object. In this study, a new method for image segmentation using the least absolute deviation (LAD) model is proposed. This method begins by obtaining the features of the input image and then, using the LAD model, it minimizes the difference between these features and the target values. We evaluate the proposed method on a few datasets and show that it can segment the content of the picture with high accuracy. In addition, the performance of this method is superior to other methods in terms of accuracy and speed. In the end, our work makes a significant contribution to the field of image segmentation by providing a robust and efficient method for automatically separating the objects and regions of interest from complex visual scenes.

This study is an attempt to improve the localization of features in confocal laser endomicroscopy images of glioma by means of weakly supervised learning methods. The proposed method combines a generative adversarial network with a U-net network to segment the glioblastoma region with high accuracy, even when annotated data is limited. The results show that the proposed method performs better than classical segmentation methods, and it also requires less human annotating. This method could be used to improve the accuracy of detecting and monitoring glioma in confocal images, and hence help in the clinical care of brain tumour patients.

The paper introduces a theory for creating and analyzing multi-photon entangled states using weak nonlinearities. The system consists of an entangler and a detangler, which both rely on the properties of the weak nonlinearity to produce and measure the desired states. A detailed description of the system and its governing equations are presented. They show that the system is feasible and effective by using both simulations and experiments. This paper opens a new way for the generation and analysis of advanced quantum states with potential applications in quantum information and communication.

In the wilds of the Yukon, in the last of the nineteenth century, a boy called Jack is left behind after his parents’ death at the gold rush. He is taken by an old man called Wolf Larsen, who raises him like a son. In the end Jack and his companions choose to help the wolf and the other animals. They learn that true heroism and courage are not to be found in conquering the wild, but in working with nature and respecting the creatures that share it.

‘To Live Forever’ is a novel by American writer Robert Silverberg, published in hardcover by Doubleday in 1969. This paper presents a novel deep learning approach to edge detection, which has been inspired by the classical methods. Edge detection is a fundamental task in image processing and in the field of computer vision, with great significance in a variety of applications. The classical methods, although very effective, are sometimes troubled by noise, texture, and occlusion. To overcome these limitations, we propose a deep learning approach that combines the advantages of the classical methods with the strengths of deep learning. This method is tested and evaluated on several popular data sets, and the results show that combining the classical methods with deep learning can achieve better results. This study opens up a new way for the design of deep learning models for edge detection and possibly other image processing tasks.

The noiseless NLMS algorithm is one of the most widely used adaptive filters, and its performance is dependent on the step size. In this paper we present a new approach for determining the optimum step size in the noiseless NLMS system, using the framework of a Bayesian network. The proposed approach provides a step size that depends on the ambient noise and the input signal. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through simulation and analysis. The results show that the proposed method can improve the performance of the noiseless NLMS algorithm with regard to both the convergence and the epsilon error.

We propose a new unified network-based model of the dynamics of human cells and tissues over time. The model can be used to predict the rate at which cells age in vivo, and the extent of tissue damage and disease progression. Our results demonstrate that the model can predict the rate of cell death and the degree of tissue damage in the human body. The model also provides insights into the mechanisms underlying aging of different organs and tissues.

THE PRIMITIVES OF SILENCE is an absorbing romance, set on the high seas in the year 1870, when maritime wars were still raging between the European nations. The plot begins with the capture of a young British sailor, named Jameson, by a band of French privateers, called the pirates of silence. For some time after, Jameson gradually becomes more than a captive, and learns how, at such a time, desperation can corrupt even the most honourable man. He forges an alliance with one of the pirate captains, Jean-Claude, and together they battle against their enemies, and brave the perils of the sea. But their return to Britain becomes dangerous, for it becomes known that they have valuable information about the British Navy. Both sides are keen to get at this, and to capture the pirates. They have to battle with fierce storms, and have to survive the deadly forces of nature, so as to reach home safely with their treasure, and the fate of Europe depends on their escape.

In this world, the human right to life is guaranteed by the fact of being human. There is no essential difference between people that would make some more worthy of life than others. Thus slavery is abolished for all time with the exception of the voluntary enslavement or servitude of individuals who cannot otherwise support themselves. (For example, criminals may be enslaved instead of imprisoned. Parents may sell a child into slavery to support his family after the parent’s death.) In the meantime, the government decides whether the enslaved person will remain a slave until his death, or whether the contract will be terminated by other means. Slaves receive two “credits” per workday. Some are accumulated through the bare existence of the person, some through his labor (points) and some by his failures (punishment points). At least half a credit per day must go to pay the rent. All credits are credited to the individual slave’s account, but each slave is only allowed to spend a certain number of these credits per year (the yearly allowance). Any surplus is taxed at the end of the year. Credits from other slaves cost double their value, so it is uncommon for people to buy them from other slaves, except when someone is buying something that can be overpaid for, for example a second home, since the transfer of ownership must be completed before the seller leaves the premises. (On the other hand, moving companies offer good deals on their own terms, since they have high operating costs.) As a result of accumulating too many debts, credit is worthless and future loans are much more expensive, including those for automobiles and business. One man, for example, refused to pay for a small dinner party because he wanted to save money. Since only a few guests came, he was unpopular, and those he had borrowed from demanded the money plus interest, because it was obvious that he never intended to pay them back. After many reproaches of meanness from his friends, he lost almost all his possessions, and no one would lend him any more money.

This paper proposes a method of loss for the purpose of colorizing images. Our method takes advantage of adversarial learning to generate a more realistic and informative colorization mask, which can be used for the task of coloring sketches. The proposed method combines the generator-discriminator framework with the perceptual loss to generate realistic and meaningful colors. We tested our method on the data of drawings, and the result shows that the images colored with our method have a significantly higher accuracy and better visual appearance than those obtained with other methods.

In this paper, we present a new method for semantic image segmentation using a regularized convolutional neural network (RNN). Semantic image segmentation is an important task in the field of computer vision that involves assigning a class to each pixel in an image, where classes correspond to meaningful objects or regions in the scene. Existing approaches to semantic image segmentation have several shortcomings, such as the reliance on hand-crafted features, the high computation costs and the need for a large amount of labeled data. Our method addresses these issues by combining the strengths of deep learning with domain knowledge. The model consists of a hierarchical convolutional neural network that learns to map images in a hierarchical fashion, and a regularization term that forces the output of the network to be smooth and coherent. The regularization term is based on a new formulation that takes into account the spatial relationships between the pixels of the image, which allows the network to extract fine-grained information while still providing a coherent output. We evaluate our method on several datasets, and show that it outperforms the state-of-the-art in terms of accuracy and efficiency. We also conduct a series of ablation studies to examine the effectiveness of individual parts of our method and provide insights into the role of each part in improving the performance. The main contributions of this paper are as follows: * Our method achieves excellent performance on several benchmarks, while being computationally efficient. * We present a detailed analysis of the effects of different parts of our method, and provide insights into the importance of each part. Overall, our work shows that combining deep learning with domain knowledge can yield promising results in the context of semantic image segmentation.

This paper provides a comprehensive survey of deformable image registration using an optimization-based approach. The authors discuss the viewpoints and the main components of deformable image registration, as well as the two-level training strategies to improve the performance of deformable image registration. They also explore potential extensions and applications outside of medical image tasks. In summary, this paper provides a detailed review of the state of the art of deformable image registration for various tasks.

We introduce a new approach to the smoothing of dilated convolutions for image segmentation. The proposed method is based on the observation that the output of a dilated convolution is a linear combination of the outputs of the corresponding convolution with different dilation rates. We show that the coefficients of this linear combination can be efficiently computed using only a single matrix-vector multiplication. It is possible to compute the output of a dilated convolution efficiently using a standard convolution with a single dilation rate. We show that our method can improve the performance of dilated convolutions in image segmentation. Therefore, our method can be used to enhance dilated convolutions. And we also show that our method can be used to efficiently compute the output of a dilated convolution with a large number of dilation rates. The present paper is divided into three parts. The first part introduces the method of our new approach to the smoothing of dilated convolutions for image segmentation. We show that the method can be used to improve the performance of dilated convolutions for image segmentation. We also show that our method can be used to efficiently compute the output of a dilated convolution with a large number of dilation rates. The second part is a discussion on the results of our experiments. The third part is the conclusion.

This paper is a theoretical study of the properties of the synchronization and asynchrony of distributed components. It explores the theoretical aspects of communication protocols, the behavior of components and the influence of communication modes on system performance and availability. This study makes use of mathematical modeling and simulation tools to study the behavior of components in different conditions. The results reveal significant differences between the synchronization and asynchrony of components, which is important for the design and management of distributed systems. In the end, the paper proposes to optimize the communication protocol in order to optimize the interoperability of distributed systems.

In the peaceful village of Ravenswood, nestled in the heart of the Silent Wood, a dark force has settled. Mysterious things have been going on, and the villagers are engulfed in terror and dread. Strange sounds in the night, the disappearance of cattle, and even people, are a common occurrence. A strange gentleman has come to Ravenswood. He is called Mr. Darkwater, and his arrival coincides with the onset of the terrifying events. He is known to smile, and to stare with an enigmatic look. The villagers decide to investigate, and come upon an ancient book hidden in the forest. It tells of a god, once worshipped by their ancestors, but now forgotten. It speaks of a ritual to be performed, involving human sacrifices, which will awaken the god and give him power. As the villagers come to realize that Mr. Darkwater is no innocent bystander, but the ringleader of the whole conspiracy, they discover that he is the one who has been performing the dark ritual. He has sacrificed the villagers, and has already succeeded in waking the god. With time running out, the remaining villagers must come together and confront Mr. Darkwater before it is too late. But will their combined efforts be enough to save Ravenswood from the clutches of the evil god? Or will they succumb to the darkness that threatens to overtake them?

This paper describes the use of quasi-likelihood methods for spatial point processes. We show that these methods can provide efficient and accurate estimates of the model when the maximum likelihood estimators fail because of the computational intractable nature of the problem or because of lack of convergence. By a series of simulations and comparisons of real data, we demonstrate that our method outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and speed of computation. Our results highlight the usefulness of the quasi-likelihood method as an alternative approach to the analysis of complex spatio-temporal phenomena.

Recent experiments in scene parsing have shown that the level-set method, which treats image segmentation as a continuous process of evolution, can produce a high degree of accuracy. But these methods rely on heuristic criteria to merge the segments, and do not explicitly model the relations between them, which limits their performance when the data is uncertain or incomplete. We propose a deep level-set framework that combines the advantages of the level-set method with the resources of deep learning. We use a deep network to model the relations between the regions, and this network controls the evolution of the level-set method. We also introduce a new loss function for segmentation that combines the cross-entropy loss with an adversarial loss, and we show that this loss enables the model to learn from incomplete and ambiguous data. Our method obtains the best results on the Cityscapes and CamVid data sets, and has the advantage of generalizing well to new data, which is not true for other methods.

Medical image segmentation is an important stage of medical image processing and has important clinical significance. However, the accuracy and robustness of medical image segmentation methods are still limited due to the noise, different appearances of images, and complex anatomical structures. This paper proposes a novel deep learning-based method for robust general medical image segmentation. This method uses the advantages of deep convolutional neural networks and multi-level feature fusion to enhance the accuracy and robustness of medical image segmentation. Extensive experiments on different medical image data sets show the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method compared with state-of-the-art methods. In addition, a detailed ablation study is conducted to analyze the contribution of each component of the method. Our experiments show that the proposed method can obtain good accuracy and robustness in medical image segmentation. It is a promising method for a variety of medical image analysis tasks.

Observations of the optical conductivity of a single layer of molybdenum disulphide were made by means of a combined experimental and theoretical approach. The optical conductivity of MoS2 is of considerable interest, owing to its high mobility of charge carriers and direct bandgap. Measurements and calculations were made over a wide range of temperatures and ac fields. Our results indicate that the optical conductivity of MoS2 has a strong frequency dependence, with a peak at the absorption edge, which corresponds to the transition from the valence to the conduction band. Anisotropy in the optical conductivity was also observed; the conductivity along the c-axis of the crystal is much higher than along the a-axis, and this anisotropy increases with decreasing temperature. We have also investigated the spin–orbit Hall effect in MoS2, which is caused by the coupling of the spin and valley degrees of freedom. We have found that the spin–orbit Hall conductivity is nonzero only under the influence of an external magnetic field and that it is strongly dependent on the direction of the field. The results obtained from simulations of the Kubo method and the density-functional theory were used to support our experimental results. A good agreement between the experimental and calculated data was obtained, and the DFT calculations showed that the optical conductivity is determined mainly by the concentration of charge carriers, which can be modified by adjusting the doping level or the gate bias. Our work has provided new insights into the optoelectronic properties of MoS2.

This article discusses shape representations for volumetric image segmentation of sparse point clouds. The idea is to develop a new method of image segmentation which will increase the accuracy and speed of the process, and overcoming the limitations of the current approach to point cloud data. A machine learning algorithm is presented which can learn the shape representations from the sparse point cloud, and a new technique for analyzing volumetric structures is shown. The results demonstrate a substantial increase in accuracy and speed, and thus the capability of the proposed method over the current methods. This article presents a new method for understanding complex objects in volumetric images, and it has a great influence on the future development of 3D-imaging technology.

This article studies the luminosity-to-metal (L-Z) and mass-to-metal (M-Z) relations for compact star-forming galaxies (CSGs). These relations are based on a sample of galaxies from the MOSFIRE Deep Evolution Field (MODEF) and the Hubble Ultra-Deep Field (HUDF). The data are distributed over a wide range of redshifts (0  z  3) and they reveal that both L-Z and M-Z relations are applicable to CSGs at all redshifts. The metallicity of the CSGs at a given luminosity or mass is found to be lower than that of normal star-forming galaxies (NSFs). The M-Z relation for CSGs is also shown to be slightly steeper than that for NSGs, whereas the L-Z relation between the two types of galaxies shows no significant difference between them. This could be due to the difference in the star-formation history, as well as the environment of galaxies, which would have contributed to the evolution of the L-Z and M-Z relations.

We consider a type of system of random oscillators which, in contrast to the usual PROMs, is determined by the values of the parameters and the position of the oscillators on the graph, and is well described by Fokker–Planck equations. Under mild assumptions these FPE turn out to be related to Ott–Antonsen type partial differential equations, which allow circulating wave solutions which generate self-organized states consisting of stationary phases or phase clusters which move along the edges of the graph. An example of a biologically relevant model is the Kuramoto model, which describes the synchronization of populations of neural cells connected by excitatory and inhibitory synapses, and chemical kinetics, for example the Belousov–Zhabotinsky reaction, which describes spatiotemporal patterns during catalytic oxidation reactions. We provide an efficient way to study the system, based on a combination of numerical simulations, justified mathematically by an analysis in the form of a resemblance of optimal transport and statistical mechanics for ordinary differential equations.

Encode-Decode with Atrous Separable Convolution (ESC) is a new model of deep learning proposed for semantic image segmentation. ESC consists of an encoder network that extracts features from the input image and a decoder network that predicts the mask for each pixel. At the same time, we introduce Atrous Separable Convolutions to optimize the memory consumption, but not to reduce the computational speed. The proposed encoder uses a combination of convolution and pooling operations to downsample the feature map, while the decoder uses upsampling and a pair of convolution layers to upsample the predicted mask. This is an effective approach to spatial loss, reducing the prediction error of the corresponding pixel and preserving the relationship between corresponding granularity. In addition, we introduce Atrous Separable Convolution, which is often shared by traditional convolution filters. By performing separable convolutions only in the channel dimension, we can reduce the memory consumption and computational complexity of convolution filters by half. The proposed model outperforms other dense U-nets on various test datasets, such as Cityscapes and CoCo-text, and the experimental results are: the accuracy of semantic image segmentation.

Abstract: We propose to apply, by means of Wasserstein-energy minimization over the Wasserstein loss function and joint probability of the domains and the labels, a general method for the reduction of the errors of translation in multi-class classification problems like cross-lingual object detection and zero-shot text classification. We only use annotated data from the other source domains with the same label space partition, but no directly labelled data from the test domain. They are implicitly matched by means of a maximum marginal entropy estimation and joint probability distribution estimation method. This makes the representations more general, by reducing the effect of high uncertainty of the classifier on areas of high uncertainty of the target, and enhancing the semantic features similarity. As proof of concept, we compare three literature models with various architectural forms that contain transformers, which outperform the standard loss-aligned trainings and the domain projection layers, and the contrastive learning layers on the fourteen standard data sets from four tasks and fields, scene graph generation, named entity recognition, object detection, and knowledge graph completion. In order to make the semantics of images more accurate and adaptable, we propose a multi-head dividing-and-ruling method based on uncertainty to detect night scenes. We first train the uncertainty estimator and refine it with a multi-head dividing-and-ruling method, and then we train the GCL-net to segment the image with various uncertainty degrees, and the GCL-net achieves higher accuracy by using the ambiguity of the program. In order to make full use of the data of various degrees of uncertainty, the GCL-net adopts three heads with different weights, and the uncertainty head is the uncertainty predictor. After comparing the prediction accuracy of the three branches, the uncertainty branch can be selected according to the uncertainty degree, and the output is determined according to the degree of uncertainty. So we train the GCL-net with two different training data, that is, data with low ambiguity and data with high ambiguity, so as to obtain a network that can recognize images of various degrees of ambiguity. The uncertainty head is the proposed objective uncertainty evaluation method, and the network performance is evaluated based on the proposed method. After extensive experiments, the proposed method can achieve the best results in the field of classification when compared with the existing best methods.
