Recent progress in deep learning has achieved excellent results in 3D medical image segmentation. However, the current method relies on a large amount of annotated data. In this paper, we present a sparse annotation strategy based on active learning for 3D medical image segmentation. Given a small number of annotated samples, our method automatically selects the most useful information to be annotated from unannotated data using attention mechanisms, and then trains the segmentation model with the new data. This approach is implemented in two steps: a global attention stage that generates a spatially weighted label map as a guidance, and a learned local attention stage that focuses on the difficult areas for fine annotation. In addition, an effective active learning strategy is introduced to sample the most informative data for annotation. We evaluate the proposed method using abdominal aortic aneurysm segmentation in 3D helical computed tomography (CT) images. We compare our method with a fully supervised learning approach and an active learning approach without attention-based data selection on two publically available sparsely annotated datasets. The results demonstrate that the proposed method is superior to the compared methods both in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

A novel approach for the segmentation of two-dimensional structures is presented in this paper. This approach relies on the ability of tensor networks to represent and represent efficiently the large-scale data and the power of the strided tensor to segment it. Then we introduce the notion of strided tensor networks and their capacity to represent efficiently and structurally large-scale data. Then we detail our approach for the segmentation of two-dimensional structures with strided tensor networks. This approach consists in first transforming the data into a strided tensor network, which allows to use the intrinsic structure of the data. Then, we apply several tensor operations to the strided tensor network in order to extract the meaningful features that will be used for the segmentation. Finally, we use these features to perform the segmentation, which, with a high accuracy and efficiency, we illustrate on several data. We show the effectiveness of our approach on several datasets and a comparison with the state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, we analyze the cost of the algorithm and show its scalability and efficiency. Our approach has a strong potential for the real-time segmentation of large-scale two-dimensional structures and can be used in fields such as: intelligent machines, robotics, medical imagery. Furthermore, it provides a fundamental framework for higher-order tensor networks and thus new opportunities for research. Finally, the method shows high accuracy and scalability, which makes it a useful tool for many applications.

This is an academic paper which introduces a novel approach to the problem of clothing identification and classification in images, and presents a joint image segmentation and labeling method that combines the advantages of both methods and can achieve higher accuracy and efficiency. In this paper, firstly, the problem of clothing identification and classification is introduced, and the state-of-the-art methods are reviewed. Then a new method of identifying and labeling images of clothes by using a deep neural network is introduced, which is combined with supervised and unsupervised learning methods and can be applied to a wide variety of clothes and patterns. Finally, the accuracy of the new method on some well-known data sets is compared with the accuracy of the state-of-the-art method. The results show that the proposed method achieves the best performance in clothing co-parsing. The unified and efficient method of clothing co-parsing by joint image segmentation and labeling is a major contribution to the field of computer vision.

Suppose that the abstract of a paper on the inverse power flow is in such terms. The inverse power flow problem is the fundamental problem of power systems, which involves finding a combination of power generation and bus voltages which results in a certain pattern of the flow of electric energy through the wires and certain voltages at the terminals of the bus. It is the basic tool of the operator and planner of power systems, who thus study and improve the operating conditions of the network. We review in this paper the mathematical formulation of the inverse power flow problem, its solution methods, and its applications. We analyze the strength and weakness of the various methods proposed for solving the inverse power flow, both linear and non-linear. We give a detailed analysis of the complexity of solving the inverse power flow and discuss the problems associated with its solution. We also give a case study illustrating the application of the inverse power flow to a real network. We show the implication of the inverse power flow on the flow of electricity in the system in various situations of generation and load and we identify potential congestion and improvement points. In this paper we present a complete overview of the inverse power flow and its role in the analysis and optimization of power systems. It is intended as a useful source of information for practitioners and research workers in power systems, and a starting point for further development of the field.

Here we propose a new method for semantic segmentation, STD2P, that uses the Spatio-Temporal Data Driven Pooling (STDP) method to learn the features of the space and time information in the color images. Unlike previous methods, which are usually based on hand-crafted features or deep neural networks, STD2P uses an unlabeled color image, which is a large number of the data in the world, and learns a rich set of features that can effectively reflect the spatial and temporal information of the images. The STD2P method is mainly composed of two parts: the STDP part and the semantic segmentation part. The STDP part aggregates the oblique red, green, and blue images into a set of spatial and temporal features by computing the statistics of the data, and the semantic segmentation part uses these features to predict the class labels of each pixel. We evaluated our method on several public oblique red, green, and blue image datasets, such as the NYUv2 and Robustlogistic datasets, and demonstrated that it outperforms other methods, which rely on hand-crafted features or deep neural networks trained with labeled data. We believe that our contribution is: (1) the proposal of a data-driven method for RGBD semantic segmentation, which uses the space and time information of the color images, (2) the development of a novel Spatio-Temporal Data Driven Pooling method to aggregate the color images into a rich set of features, and (3) the new top performance of the oblique red, green, and blue image datasets with our STD2P method., large-scale unlabeled data can be used to train deep learning models for color images, and the accuracy of the classification of color images is improved.

This paper presents the development and implementation of a mixed-supervised deep neural network for medical image segmentation. It aims to address the challenges in the automated processing of a large number of medical images, which are limited in labeled data for supervised learning. It combines the knowledge obtained from unsupervised learning with the limited amount of supervised data to improve the accuracy of the segmentation. The performance of the system has been demonstrated by experiments conducted on several different types of medical images. The experiments show a significant improvement over conventional methods. This study makes a significant contribution to the field of medical images and machine learning by establishing a novel method combining unsupervised and supervised learning. The proposed method improves the precision of medical image segmentation and has the potential to enhance the accuracy of diagnosis and treatment planning in various health care settings.

The seeded laplacian method is a novel method for segmenting images, whose inputs are marks drawn on a surface. Using a local Gaussian operator as a seed, the method is capable of accurately segmenting images in a way that allows the operator to provide the best guidance in a human-guided manner. This method offers a quick and efficient solution to the problem of image segmentation, and is particularly suited to applications where real-time feedback is essential. This paper is based on extensive experimental results that have demonstrated the efficiency of this method. Using this method as a basis, the researcher has developed an interactive image segmentation system that offers a solution to the problem of real-time image segmentation, and it can be applied to a wide range of applications.

This paper introduces SynSeg-Net, a new deep learning model for synthetic segmentation without the need for the target modality. Using the power of GANs to generate synthetic images that mimic the target modality, our method uses synthetic images to train a segmentation model. We propose a new loss function that encourages the segmentation model to learn from synthetic images without the need for the target modality. We compare our method with state-of-the-art methods that require the target modality and show that our method can outperform these methods. Our work has important implications for medical image segmentation, where obtaining high-quality annotated data is expensive and difficult.

The Casimir force is a fundamental phenomenon of physics which is the result of quantum fluctuations of the electro-magnetic field. Precise measurements of the Casimir force are important for testing theoretical calculations and for understanding the underlying physics. In this paper, we explore the potential of non-contact atomic force microscopy (NC-AFM) for future measurements of the Casimir force. NC-AFM is a powerful method for the microscopic manipulation and observation of a wide variety of materials without making contact. We discuss the advantages of NC-AFM for Casimir force measurements, including its scalability and its ability to reduce systematic errors. We also discuss the difficulties and limitations of using NC-AFM for Casimir force measurements, such as the necessity for accurate calibration and the effect of surface roughness. Despite these challenges, we conclude that NC-AFM has the potential to make major advances in Casimir force measurement, and in so doing to shed light on the nature of the Casimir force.

This paper presents a novel method of finger vein recognition, which uses the uniqueness of the codes to identify individuals based on their finger vein pattern. The method combines image processing with machine learning to generate unique codes for each individual’s finger vein pattern. The codes can be used to identify individuals and thus constitute a reliable and efficient method of biometric recognition. The method is divided into three stages: image acquisition, code generation, and recognition. In the image acquisition stage, the finger vein pattern is captured by a specialized camera and then processed to enhance the visibility of the veins and remove noise. In the code generation stage, the unique codes for each individual’s finger vein pattern are generated using machine learning and image processing. In the recognition stage, the codes generated are compared with the stored codes in the database to identify the individual. This method has several advantages over previous methods of finger vein recognition, including improved accuracy, speed, and security. The use of unique codes to recognize individuals eliminates the need to extract features and compare them, thereby greatly simplifying the process and increasing the speed of identification. In addition, the codes generated by this method are safe and reliable, and it is difficult for unauthorized users to guess or duplicate them. The experiments on a set of finger vein images show the effectiveness of this method, and the accuracy is up to 98.6%. The experiments also show that this method is robust to lighting, finger pose, and partial occlusion. It can therefore be used in real-world applications. In conclusion, this method of finger vein recognition by generating codes is a novel and effective approach to biometric recognition and a new combination of image processing and machine learning. This method has wide application, such as for access control, identity verification, and border control.

"Distributed clustering and learning over networks - a collection of algorithms and methods for dividing a large number of objects into small clusters and extracting useful information from the data, while running on different devices in a network. This approach makes efficient use of computational resources and allows parallelization of clustering and learning processes. This paper reviews some of the most popular distributed clustering methods and their variants, focusing on their efficiency, scalability, and convergence properties. The paper also presents some of the challenges and open issues in this area of research. Finally, the paper examines the applications of distributed clustering and learning in big data analysis, data compression, and machine learning over networks.

This paper is devoted to the stability of the topological properties of a bilayer of bismuth (111), a promising material for the quantum spin Hall effect. Using first principles calculations, we analyze the structural, electronic and topological properties of the bilayer in different deformations. The topological phase is preserved under all deformations, the band inversion and the nontrivial band gap are maintained. We also find a critical strain above which the system switches to the trivial phase. These results give an insight into the strain-tunable topological properties of a bismuth bilayer on (111) and open up prospects for the use of this material in future spintronics devices.

THE frame problem has been recognised as a major problem in natural language processing, since it is difficult to assign a frame to a sentence without explicit or implicit indication of a frame. In this paper, we propose a new approach to frame determination based on a combination of semantic role labelling and supervised machine learning. The results show that our approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
